numerical errors in mesh generation (e.g. for axisymmetric models). For the time being,
only the PATRAN interface supports this parameter.

2.6 The EXEC section

BUCKling ANalysis

Remarks:
1. The geometrical stiffness is computed through the displacement state of a previously
performed computation. This state is selected by using $INSERT VARIANT (see pp.
3-525) within the system variant of the current situation. The geometric stiffness matrix
is calculated automatically and must not be requested by $ADDMATRIX. The appropriate
loading state is selected using $ELSTATE LOAD.
2. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A continuation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.

4. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output the
original (stiffness orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page 2-25).
5. The given load scale factor limits are compared with the magnitude of the computed
factors, e.g. specifying SIGN = NEGATIVE FACTOR = 1.0, 3.0 yields load scale factors
between −1.0 and −3.0 .
6. If two load factor limits are given, they define an interval. All modes with load scale factors
within this interval are computed. The specification of two factors must be combined with
SIGN = POSITIVE or SIGN = NEGATIVE. Load scale factor intervals are recommended
for experienced users only.
7. The shifted algorithm which is enabled by KSHIFT = AUTO may yield much better convergence. It is therefore recommended to be used especially if many iterations are needed
to reach convergence.
Example:
Please refer to Example BA1 of [um550] on page 6-3 ff. Below a schematic example for the
UCI and the additional input needed to perform a buckling analysis is presented.

UCI-File
! -------------------------------------------! Buckling Analysis Example
! -------------------------------------------!
new
exec
!
! Static Analysis to get displacement state
!
activate situation=static
task
static
!

Remarks:
1. COMBINE allows to superimpose results referring to loading pattern or time steps by
application of predefined combination rules.
2. The combination rules are defined in the data input using $COMBINE RESULTS (see
page 3-1003 ff.) within the result specification bracket.
3. The result combination is performed for the active configuration.
4. If combined results contain any results of non-linear analyses or of analyses with contacts,
the combined result columns are in general no longer valid results and should be used
only with extreme caution.
5. If a rule refers to foreign situations, the situations must have been scanned, even if the rule
is not used by an UCI command. The use of named result variants is therefore strongly
recommended to avoid unintended reference to a rule.
6. In situ operations (omitting the RESULT option) are only allowed, if the rule refers to
the current situation only and the analysis is linear. The following points apply to in situ
operations:
(a) The item DISPlacement may be overwritten as long as no secondary results have
been calculated so far. All derived results (e.g. reaction forces, stresses) will then
be computed using the combined patterns.
(b) In situ operations on standard results are only possible as long as no derived quantities have been computed from the primary results. Therefore secondary results
cannot be combined in situ.
(c) As an exception, element stresses may be combined without using the RESULT
parameter. Then nodal point stresses may be computed afterwards containing the
combined patterns (by using the GENerate command (see page 2-152)).
(d) For in situ operations, N EW P AT = ON LY can not be applied.
(e) In situ combination of non-linear results may be enabled by UCI switch NLCOMBINE,
but see remark 4.

DIRECT ELECTRO [DYNAMIC]

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

Remarks:
1. The integration parameters α (ALPHA, SET/SHOW see page 2-25), β (BETA, SET/SHOW
see page 2-25) and δ (DELTA, SET/SHOW see page 2-35) for the direct integration may
be modified using the SET command (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. If δ is changed, the Hilber
Hughes Taylor method is used as integration method instead of the Newmark family of
methods. In this case α and β are modified internally in order to get an unconditional
stable algorithm.
2. When using nonlinear elements, the algorithm is no longer unconditional stable, so the
time step has to be selected carefully.

UCI
EXEC

3. The XY-data are prepared for the currently active node set, which should be activated
within the task mode before specifying the direct integration command.

The nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
solution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
is performed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied.
Remarks:
1. In nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.
2. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
GENerate command within the same TASK as the DIRECT NLTEMP command.
3. An additional selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the variant using
$NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the final solution and the initial values (at TSTART) are
available.
4. If DIRECT NLTEMP, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, the current
results will be generated and exported for each time step contained in the list given by
$NLRESULTS plus the final solution. Initial values (at TSTART) are not available.
5. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
the SELECT section.
6. If constant temperature modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of
the conductivity matrices. Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the singular
modes is printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extremum
values as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a
local or a global effect has been detected.
If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
the constant temperature modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the
postprocessor. There they may be evaluated in more detail.
The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command or the setting
may be included in the default definition file.
7. The setting of a minimum time increment is a break-off criterion for the iteration. If the
actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The criterion

2-126

DIRECT NLTEMP

should be applied only with great care, since for a highly nonlinear material behaviour, a

through this parameter, which can lead to larger (or smaller) computational effort.

Parameter

DIRECT NLTIME

DIRECT NLTIME

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

Description:
The nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
solution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
is performed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied. The material law is integrated on
element level at the Gauss points by various techniques.
Remarks:
1. Unsupported element types are treated as linear (material and geometry). A table of
supported elements can be found on page 5-16ff. of [um550].
2. In a nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.

UCI
EXEC

3. A combination of PLASTIC/VPLASTIC and NLELASTIC material is not supported, even
if assigned to different elements. A table of possible material combinations can be found
on page 5-16ff. of [um550].
4. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
GENerate command within the same TASK as the DIRECT NLTIME command.
5. Secondary results like stresses and strains are calculated at the Gauss points and assigned (not extrapolated) to the element nodes.
6. A selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the result variant using
$NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the final solution is available.
7. If DIRECT NLTIME, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, results will
only be generated and exported if the current load step is contained in the list given by
$NLRESULTS.
8. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
the SELECT section.
9. Initial conditions may be specified using the $INIVAL definitions in order to continue or to
refine an analysis.
10. The definition of a time dependent load $TRANSLOAD is required for the analysis.
11. Existing non-symmetric material stiffnesses (non-associative plasticity) are always symmetrized.
12. The setting of a minimum time increment TMIN is a break-off criterion for the iteration.
If the actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The
criterion should be applied only with great care, since for a highly nonlinear material
behaviour, a small time step does not imply convergence.
13. The default value for TEND = 1.0 is overwritten as soon as a result variant using $NLRESULTS
STEPS = LIST is given. In this case the time TEND is equal to the maximum time given
in the result variant.

2.6 The EXEC section

FSCoupled VIBration [ANalysis]

Description:
For the solution of the coupled eigenvalue problem, two methods are provided.
1. The Mobility-Flexibility (MF) Formulation,
which is obtained by a force formulation of the eigenvalue problem, leading to an inverse
mass (or mobility) and an inverse stiffness.

For the reader’s convenience some guidelines for deciding whether to use the MF- or the SMFormulation shall be summarized subsequently.
When the coupled system has neither rigid body modes nor constant pressure modes both
methods are equivalent. If the fluid is incompressible and has no surface waves, the SMFormulation might be more efficient. Since the compressibility matrix is zero its Cholesky factor
need not be computed and the operations involving it can be skipped. If, on the contrary, the
mass of the solid structure is so small compared to the mass of the fluid that it can be neglected,
the MF-Formulation is the better method for now the operations involving the Cholesky factor
of the mass matrix can be skipped.
If the coupled system has rigid body modes but no constant pressure modes it is beyond doubt
that the SM-Formulation should be used in order to avoid the problems caused by the singular
coupling term. For the same reasons the MF-Formulation is the appropriate method when
the coupled system has constant pressure modes but no rigid body modes. Remember that
the MF-Formulation must be used if the coupled system has constant pressure modes and a
vanishing compressibility matrix.
If the coupled system has both rigid body modes and constant pressure modes, the singular
coupling term is present as well in the MF-Formulation as in the SM-Formulation. Provided it is
not necessary to use the MF-Formulation because of a zero compressibility matrix that method
should be adopted that allows to approximate the singular coupling term. Should this not be
possible select the MF-Formulation when the number of unknowns of the fluid is small, and the
SM-Formulation if the number of unknowns of the solid structure is small.
The selection of the appropriate method is illustrated by table T2-47.

Table T2-47: Selection of the Appropriate Method
Remarks:
1. System matrix and coupling matrix generation is included in the command request.
2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the number of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively.
3. Multilevel dynamic reduction is based on a decomposition of the active component in subcomponents and the solution of a dynamically (Craig-Bampton) reduced substructure.
See also default parameters MLDRFAC, DEFAULT see page 2-72 and MLDRSIZE, DEFAULT see page 2-73. Furthermore the UCI switch MLDRFSTA, SET/SHOW see page
2-40 defines the amplification factor on top component level for the DISP/PRES eigenvalue analyses.
4. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
(see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. Those parameters are:
• ADDVEC, SET/SHOW see page 2-25
• MAXBOX, SET/SHOW see page 2-39
• CHEBEXP, SET/SHOW see page 2-34
However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter
ADDVEC should only be increased if the frequency limit is used.
5. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output the
original (stiffness orthonormalized) modes, set switch MODENORM off (see page 2-25).
6. The structural mass may be ignored, if it is small compared to the fluid mass. The mass
matrix is needed if the MF-Formulation is used to analyze a system with rigid body modes.

7. In case of incompressible fluids, the compressibility matrix vanishes. The compressibility matrix is needed if the SM-Formulation is used to analyze a system with constant
pressure modes.
8. Mechanical modes are complemented by mode shapes, induced by fluid modes. One
additional structure mode per fluid mode is generated. Applicable for fluid dominated
models with very flexible structural behavior. In this case, the MLDRPFAC switch may be
set explicitly and the MLDRFAC setting might be reduced.

10. The definition of a node set for MLDR is mandatory, if several disconnnected regions exist
(i.e. separate fluid domains).

Generation of secondary results

GENerate (DOFTYPE = DISP)

Remarks:
1. Primary results must have been computed previously.

UCI
EXEC

2. Generate stresses via the Smooth Patch Recovery method. This method is based on a
least square fit of a polynomial stress ansatz using stresses at a number of superconvergent stress points within a patch of elements. Each patch consists of a corner node
and the connected elements. Hence, SPR stresses can only be determined within elements with at least one corner node located in the interior of the mesh. SPR stresses
are available for the following element families: flange, membrane, solid, shell, solid shell,
axisymmetric membrane and axisymmetric solid. See section 6.3.1.
3. This generate command must be placed within the same task as the primary command
request to get the full history selected by $NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the last state is
available.
4. Note: GENerate ELement STRESS with ESET option should be put in a separate task.
If a previous command in the same task (e.g. STATIC) creates implicitly elemental displacements, the application of the element filter will affect these and all derived results.

This is special command to calculate statistics of time history stress results while saving disk
space for the therefor needed stresses/stress resultants. I.e. after a preceeding MODAL
TIMEhistory (or MODAL FSCoupled TIMEhistory) a GENerate MODAL TimeHistory STATistics
can be used to compute modal stresses/resultants and performing a statistical evaluation in the
time domain on-the-fly (without actually storing time domain stresses/resultants) – only the statistical data is saved to disk.
Statistical results are generated for the ESET specified here – completely independent of the
PRIMRES parameter of the MODAL TIMEhistory command (as an alternative the stress/force
statistics can also be calculated in the time domain together with the EVALuation command –
then also relying on the PRIMRES parameter).
For each element, 10 sets of statistical results are calculated as documented for the STATISTICS rule of the EVALuation command, see p. 2-298. The contents of each set depend on
element type and result:
• MTSIG: stress invariants for shell, solid shell and solid elements

GENerate (DOFTYPE = DISP)

Nodal point effective strain

Effective nodal point strain is the result of a nonlinear analysis. This generate command must
be placed within the same task as the primary command request to get the full history selected
by $NLRESULTS. Otherwise only the last state is available.
The nodal point format for effective strains consists of three quantities, for volume and for solid
shell elements: mean value, minimum value and maximum value of the scalar quantity at the
nodal point. Please note, that this result will no longer fulfill the material law due to the location
at the node and due to the averaging process.
PLASTIC:
ELASTIC:
CREEP:

Effective plastic strain value
Effective elastic strain value
Effective creep strain value

Nodal point strain
GENerate Nodal Point STRAIN

Calculation of average strain at nodal point.
Please note the following inconsistencies:
Element strain equals the total strain when calculated in a linear analysis, but equals the difference of total strain and initial strain (ε = εt − εi ) when calculated in a nonlinear analysis.
Nodal point strain and the derived principal strains are always calculated from the total strain.

GENerate (DOFTYPE = TEMP)

Generation of secondary results

GENerate (DOFTYPE = TEMP)

Cutting flux

CUTTING FLUX computes the internal heat flow if at least an element set filter is ACTIVE. The
result is given in units of power.
A boundary may be described by defining an active node set in addition, connected to the
elements of the element set. In this case the result represents the flow through the boundary.
The element set defines which side of the boundary and therefore the sign of the flow values.
The sum of the calculated flow values at nodes is written automatically to the result file. The
calculation of the internal heat flow may be invoked several times, previous results will be
overwritten.

Heat flow
GENerate HEAT FLOW

Nodal point heat flux vector in units of power/area:
q̇λ = −λ∇T

with convectivity λ and temperature T .

Description:
The solution calculates the displacements of a free body under static and inertia forces by a
quasi-static solution. As in the standard inertia relief procedure, absolute displacements are
being calculated.
The procedure calculates the inertia forces corresponding to the applied load, i.e. those inertia
forces that generate the opposite reaction forces as the applied loads. The inertia forces are
added to the applied loads and the displacements are calculated under the assumption that the
structure is rigidly restrained at the determinate supports.

Remarks:
1. The command GINERT is not needed any longer. All features were included into the
INERTIA RELIEF analysis.
2. The user selects kinematically determinate supports and specifies the related degrees of
freedom as $RIGMODE (see page 3-377 ff.).
3. The static loads are applied as usual. Additional, nonlinear (displacement dependent
loads) may be introduced with the $LCMATRIX (see page 3-835 ff.) statement.
4. The user may define break points through the definition of the end points of the analysis. The break points are given through the command alternatives within the PERMAS
command.

UCI
EXEC

5. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined.
6. The complete loads including the inertia forces (but not the displacement dependent
loads) are stored in book UBLIR.
7. If rigid body modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the system
and load matrices. Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the rigid body
modes is printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extremum
values as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a
local or a global effect has been detected.
If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postprocessor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.
8. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and interface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
into account only for the solution of the eigenvalue problem and the subsequent effective
mass computation, the structural mass matrix remains unchanged.
9. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and interface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is added to
the structural mass and is valid for all subsequent computations using the same system
matrices.
10. The selection of an iterative solution method is especially of interest, if the resulting system matrix is nonsymmetric (due to loading contribution).
11. An important setting to save disc space is the GINERTFLEX = OFF setup.

INERTIA [RELIEF]

Starting time for analysis, only applicable for contact

Description:
The solution calculates the displacements of a free body under static and inertia forces by a
quasi-static solution. This procedure is known as ’inertia relief’.
The procedure calculates the inertia forces corresponding to the applied load, i.e. those inertia
forces that generate the opposite reaction forces as the applied loads. The inertia forces are
added to the applied loads and the displacements are calculated such that they do not contain
any rigid body motions.
Remarks:
1. The model must contain rigid body modes, which may either be determined automatically
or explicitly be specified by the user with $RIGMODE.
The deprecated way of specification by $EXTERNAL is no longer possible.
2. The static loads are applied as usual, but a loading variant is expected to be present also
for all subcomponents, since the analysis creates additional loads.
3. The user may define break points through the definition of the end points of the analysis. The break points are given through the command alternatives within the PERMAS
command.
4. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined.
5. The static loads are applied as usual. Additional displacement dependent loads may be
introduced with the $LCMATRIX (see page 3-835 ff.) statement.
6. If a load history (i.e. $NLLOAD) is given the calculation is performed in the quasi-time
domain from TSTART to TEND, with the default values:
TSTART = min time from $NLLOAD and/or $NLRESULTS,
TEND = max. time from $NLRESULTS if existing, from $NLLOAD otherwise.
Note that the UCI parameter TSTART and TEND can only limit the time range of the
pre-defined load history from $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS, respectively, i.e. it is not
possible to add new additional time steps by this option.

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-199

UCI
EXEC

2.6 The EXEC section

INERTIA [RELIEF]

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

7. The complete loads including the inertia forces are stored in book UBLIR.
8. If rigid body modes were specified with $RIGMODE and additional rigid body modes
occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the system and load matrices.
Furthermore a summary of book URBM containing the unspecified rigid body modes is
printed on the result file. The summary contains the nodes having the extreme values as
well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a local or a
global effect has been detected.
If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with

ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

UCI
EXEC

9. If REFERENCE is set to CENTER, the displacements are determined such that the center
of gravity does not move. For partially supported structures, the center of the moving part
is kept in place. No $RIGMODE definition is required for REFERENCE = CENTER.
If REFERENCE is set to RIGMODE, the displacements are determined such that the
degrees of freedom specified by $RIGMODE are not moving. If no $RIGMODE is given,
the computation aborts with an error.
The deformation only differs by rigid body motions for both settings of REFERENCE.
Therefore secondary results such as stresses are identical.
10. The number of rigid body modes NOFRBM must only be specified if they shall be detected
automatically and the number is not six.
If the rigid body modes are defined with $RIGMODE, the parameter NOFRBM is not
needed.
11. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and interface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
into account only for the solution of the inertia relief problem, the structural mass matrix
remains unchanged.
12. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and interface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is added to
the structural mass and is valid for all subsequent computations using the same system
matrices.

Remarks:
1. The reliability analysis is done in an own situation, referring to analyses which are to be
included in the reliability analysis process.
2. For the time being, the analyses
• STATIC
• VIBration ANalysis
• MODAL FREQuency
• MODAL COMPLEX
• MODAL ROTATING
may be referred to in a reliability analysis.

UCI
EXEC

3. All failure functions defined in the reliability situation are processed, each leading to a
complete reliability analysis.
4. During simulation, after each sample the reliability data are written on files < project >.beta
(reliability index), < project >.cov (coefficient of variation) and < project >.pf (probability
of failure).
5. The reliability analysis for one failure function is stopped if one of the following conditions
is fulfilled:
• The reliability is determined with the desired covariance of simulation.
• The number of simulations for the actual failure function exceeds the number defined
by parameter SIMUL.
• The total number of simulations exceeds the maximum number of task loops.

8. The iterative solver is available for symmetric and non-symmetric problems with constant
damping and stiffness matrices. Exception: Diagonal frequency-dependent Control-6
elements are supported. The iterative solver is especially fast for many excitation frequencies and a limited number of load cases per excitation frequency. The accuracy can
be controlled with the ACCuracy option, the default value is 4.0, leading to a residual error
of 10−4 = 0.01%.
9. The solution scheme is recommended for a large modal basis and only few discrete viscous damping elements. It is applicable if:
• The viscous damping matrix is constant, symmetric and positive-semidefinite. Exception: Frequency-dependent symmetric Control-6 elements are supported.
• There are no additional (symmetric or quadratic) stiffness contributions.
• Elemental structural damping is not frequency dependent.
• There is no viscous damping in subcomponents (for MLDR CONF = TOP: All viscous
damping elements must be in the top component).
• Control elements may have frequency dependent stiffness, structural- or viscous
damping.
The inversion is performed using the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury (SMW) formulation.
10. The system option allows to prepare condensation matrices of a component with external
dofs for a subsequent export. Condensed loads are only prepared for the system option.
11. If several dynamic load cases shall be analyzed in the same job, the use of an assembly
situation should be considered for performance reasons. System and result variant must
be identical, only the loading variant may differ. See $SITUATION and example DRA3V2.

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-211

UCI
EXEC

5. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
may be calculated only in single components.
At least one set (node or element set) must be active when applying the -REDUCEDcommand option.

Remarks:
1. The command performs a sweep over rotational velocities defined in the result variant
($ROTSPEED (see page 3-1066 ff.), see section 3.2.7). XY-data for a Campbell diagram
are prepared: eigenfrequencies (RSFRQ), damping coefficients (RSDMP) and equivalent
viscous damping ratio (RSDRT).
2. A free vibration analysis must have been performed previously to this command. The
subsequent modal complex analysis may be grouped within the same task as the vibration
analysis in order to scan the whole computational task.
3. After the modal complex eigenvalue calculation, the situation used for the free vibration
analysis will be active.

UCI
EXEC

4. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
may be calculated only in single components.
At least one set (node or element set) must be active when applying the -REDUCEDcommand option.
5. For a large number of complex modes, FREQLIMB is an option to save disc space and
elapsed time.
6. The backtransformation filters UNSTABLE and POSREL may be combined. They are
complementary to the optional frequency limit.
7. If no eigenmode fulfils the given selection (e.g. only unstable modes selected but there is
no unstable mode), then the first eigenmode is kept.
8. For the generation of XY-data for a Campbell diagram always the complete set of complex eigenfrequencies is used, frequency limit and backtransformation filters UNSTABLE
and POSREL are ignored. So the numbering of XY-data sets and the selected set of
eigenvectors may be different.
9. For RFREQ=EIGFREQ the computation of equivalent viscous damping is performed with
the eigenfrequency of each mode, instead of a constant reference frequency.

Remarks:

2. After the modal time history analysis, the situation used for the free vibration analysis will
be active.
3. The integration parameters α , β and δ for the integration rules may be modified using the
SET command (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. However, those parameters
should be modified only with great care. If δ is changed, the Hilber Hughes Taylor method
is used as integration method instead of the newmark family of methods. In this case α
and β are modified internally in order to get an unconditional stable algorithm.
4. When using nonlinear elements, the algorithm is no longer unconditional stable, so the
time step has to be selected carefully.
5. The xy-data are prepared for the currently active node set, which should be activated
within the task mode before specifying the modal time history command.
6. The xy-data are always related to the component system. The command TRANSFORM
(see page 2-325 ff.) in conjunction with XYDATA (see page 2-327 ff.) can be used in order
to extract results in a local coordinate system.
7. Initial conditions may be specified using the $INIVAL definitions (see page 3-832) in order
to continue or to refine an analysis.
8. If PRIMRES=REDUCED has been selected, the nodal point results are computed for
all nodes, referred by the active node set or the active element set. Secondary results
for elements are possible, if an element set has been activated previously. Primary and
secondary results in subcomponents are not available. Residuals and reaction forces
may be calculated only in single components.
At least one set (node or element set) must be active when applying the -REDUCEDcommand option.
9. PRIMRES=NONE can drastically reduce disk space in case the MODAL TIMEhistory is
just used as a predecessor for a succeeding GENerate MODAL TIMEhistory STATistics
or GENerateFATIGUE analysis only and no actual time domain results are needed (i.e.
if MODAL TIMEhistory is used to just generate the modal time participation factors).

Explanation
The material has only plastic deformations.
The material has only visco-plastic deformations.
The material has nonlinear elastic properties.
The material has creep deformations.

The nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
solution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
is performed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied. The material law is integrated on
element level at the Gauss points by various techniques.
The definition nodes for the rigid body mode decoupling should be selected such, that they are
not within the plastic zone.
Remarks:
1. NLINERTIA requires the existence of rigid body modes. The rigid body modes must be
defined with $RIGMODE. Together with the other constraints, the $RIGMODE definitions
must yield a statically determinate support.
2. The options are inherited from the underlying NLMATERIAL command. Please also look
there for remarks. Their description is not repeated here.

Description:

UCI
EXEC

The nonlinear analysis is realized through a piecewise linear computation. A general nonlinear
solution procedure with line searches is used for the solution. In each loading step, an iteration
is performed until the given convergence criterion is satisfied. The material law is integrated on
element level at the Gauss points by various techniques.
Remarks:
1. Unsupported element types are treated as linear (material and geometry). This will affect
results especially for NLGEOM = YES! A table of supported elements may be found on
page 5-16ff. of [um550].
2. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined. Please refer
to Example CA1 of [um550] on page 4-103 ff.
3. In a nonlinear analysis, each situation must be analyzed in a separate TASK.
4. A combination of PLASTIC/VPLASTIC and NLELASTIC material is not supported, even
if assigned to different elements. A table of possible material combinations can be found
on page 5-16ff. of [um550].
5. Secondary results (including residual and reaction forces) must be computed using the
GENERATE (see page 2-152 ff.) command within the same TASK as the NLMATERIAL
command.
6. By default, secondary results like stresses and strains are calculated at the Gauss points
and assigned (not extrapolated) to the element nodes. Use DEFAULT SET EXSLEN and
EXSNEN to request extrapolation.
7. A selection of result steps may be done in the data input of the result variant using
$NLRESULTS (see page 3-1053 ff.). Otherwise only the final solution is available.
8. If NLMATERIAL, GENerate and EXPORT are performed in a TASK loop, results will
only be generated and exported if the current load step is contained in the list given
by $NLRESULTS.
9. XY-results may be extracted from the history information using the XYDATA command of
the SELECT section.

2-248

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

2.6 The EXEC section

NLMATERIAL

10. If rigid body modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the stiffness
matrices, if the direct solution method is used. Furthermore a summary of book URBM
containing the rigid body modes is printed on the result file. The summary contains the
nodes having the extremum values as well as the summation over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a local or a global effect has been detected.
If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postprocessor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66
ff.) or the setting may be included in the default definition file.

12. The setting of a minimum time increment is a break-off criterion for the iteration. If the
actual time increment is below the given value, the process is terminated. The criterion
should be applied only with great care, since for a highly nonlinear material behavior, a
small time step does not imply convergence.
13. When a combined geometrical and material nonlinear analysis is performed the geometric
nonlinear part is treated with the co-rotational theory. No coordinate updates are done.
14. The Thomas acceleration can be used solely for plastic and viscoplastic models (MAT =
PLASTIC/VPLASTIC) in a geometric linear analysis (NLGEOM = NO).
For models containing HEXE8 elements it is important to replace them by HEXFO8 elements, since the Thomas method is not suitable for elements with internal degrees of
freedom.
15. Without further specifications, the default value is TEND = 1.0.
With $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS given in the data input, the default value for TEND is
the maximum time given in the result variant by $NLRESULTS.
If the TEND parameter is specified, it defines the final time of the analysis independent of
the settings in the data input.
16. In the predictor step, convergence is always checked with the force criterion, the selection
is only considered in the corrector step. The actual values are printed to the log file.

Remarks:
1. Contact analysis may be performed in STATIC, INERTIA RELIEF and NLMATERIAL analyses. In case of NLMATERIAL, or if design constraints CAGAPS, CAPRES or CAREAC
(see $DCONSTRAINT on page 3-898 ff.) are used in the optimization, only optimization
methods working with the option DSMETHOD = NONE may be used.
2. Property values ($GEODAT) dependent on design variables may be prepared as elemental post-processing result by GENerate EPRES, see example OP15. The updated coordinates of a shape optimization are available as result by ITEM COORdinate CHANGE

OPTIM

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

respectively COORdinate MODification. A model with updated coordinates may be exported by ITEM MODL NEWCOOR. See example OP6.
3. The parameter TOLDV may be used as alternative convergence criterion (instead of
CSTVIOL). If set, for convergence it is required that the maximum relative change of the
design variables in the last iteration is below the given value. An application are problems
which have no feasible solution.
4. Switching between DSMETHOD = DIRECT and ADJOINT is only possible for STATIC,
INERTIA RELIEF, MODAL FREQuency and TEMPerature analyses. The selection of the
most efficient method is also dependent on the available disk space. If a large number of
design variables is defined, the direct method may be limited by the fact, that each design
variable will cause a full right hand side. In this case, the adjoint variable method might
help (at computing time costs for a large number of constraints).

UCI
EXEC

5. Methods of the “AOS” module may be used also with DSMETHOD = NONE. For gradient
based methods, derivatives will then be calculated by difference quotient, leading to an
extra analysis for each design variable.
6. Optimization including design elements of type DBEAD, DFREE and DTOPO (see
$DELEMENT) is not possible with DSMETHOD = NONE.
7. The ACP method uses a more conservative constraint approximation than e.g. the convex approximation scheme and is recommended for highly nonlinear behavior. This may
be caused by manufacturing restrictions or also by constraints like frequency response
quantities. It is also quite well suited for very large optimization problems, since it has
out-of-core capabilities.
8. The Global Domain Centering (GDC) approach looks for a sphere with maximum diameter inside the feasible region, not for a single optimal solution point. Use DSMETHOD =
NONE for this option.
9. The Locally improved Dividing Rectangle (LDR) algorithm is a derivative free method
to detect a global extremum. It is suited for a small number of design variables. Use
DSMETHOD = NONE to save computation time. Requires the “AOS” module. Exhausting
the maximal number of loops is the only termination criterion for this method.
10. The MultiStart (MS) method uses local optimizers with several starting points. It requires
the “AOS” module. This method exhausts the maximal number of loops. Termination
of the underlying local optimizers can be controlled by the parameters TOLOBJ and
CSTVIOL. The following specific settings may be changed by UCI command DEFAULT
SET:
• OPTMSUBMETH
• OPTMSEED
11. The Optimality Criteria (OC) method is a derivative free method for nodal point stresses.
The usage of DFREE design elements is mandatory, see example OP19.
Besides stress as constraint or objective, further design constraints may be defined if
analytical derivatives are available.

2-256

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

2.6 The EXEC section

OPTIM

12. The convergence of the SCP algorithm may be influenced by UCI command DEFAULT
SET OPTCVXMODE. Often, convex linearization (1) will lead to a smaller number of
iterations, while MMA (0) may be advantageous for higher nonlinear problems.
13. The Wedge-constrained Linear programming (WLIN) method is a derivative free method,
use DSMETHOD = NONE to save computation time. Requires the “AOS” module.
14. The termination criteria for the methods of the “AOS” module are different from the default
convergence criteria:

• The convergence criterion is not applied, if the algorithm is in some special phase,
e.g. initial sampling or construction of finite differences. The WLIN method has a
sampling phase during the first (designvariables + 1) loops.
• All the local methods are Trust Region methods, i.e., they adaptively control the
step size. These methods are designed to guarantee convergence to some point
which may be a solution of the optimization problem or not. The latter case is called
unsuccessful convergence.
• Successful convergence is reached when
|f (best) − f (k) | < otol · |f (best) | and
(k)
cj - c̄j < cviol · |c̄j |, j = 1 . . . m.
Note that the current objective function value is compared to the objective value of
the best known point and not to the value of the last point (which is the default when
a non-“AOS” method is selected).
• Unsuccessful convergence is reached whenever
– the relative step size is smaller than the parameter TOLDV
– and the successful convergence criterion is not satisfied
– and the algorithm is not in some special phase, e.g. initial sampling or construction of finite differences.
The default value for “AOS” methods is TOLDV=1.0E-5.
15. The following default switches control the advanced optimization solvers (AOS):
• OPTSUBTOL
• OPTPENAL0
• OPTPENAL1
• OPTRUSTSIZ0 and OPTRUSTSIZ1

loops.

Remarks:

RESONANT ANalysis

3. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
(see page 2-25) before starting the analysis. Those parameters are:
• ADDVEC
• MAXBOX
• CHEBEXP
However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter

UCI
EXEC

5. Further parameters are active in case of the iterative solver, namely:
• MAXITS
• TOLITS
• MBLKITS
• THETA
• ZETA
• RBMITS
• MAXNIT
They may be modified using the SET command (see page 2-25) before starting the analysis.
6. The iterative solver is restricted to diagonal conductivity matrices, hence only the diagonal mass approach is possible and no MPC-conditions or substructuring models may be
treated for the time being.
7. The usage of the iterative solution method may be advantageous especially in case of
good conditioned structures. The saving of disk storage is especially for larger models
considerably, since only an incomplete decomposition of the stiffness matrix is performed.
8. Rigid body modes are treated different by using the iterative solver. The direct solver
separates the rigid body modes (as far as detected) from elastic modes of the structure,
whereas the iterative method computes the rigid body modes like elastic modes.

STATIC

3. If rigid body modes occur, the analysis is terminated after the calculation of the stiffness
matrices. Furthermore a summary of the rigid body modes is printed on the result file.
The summary contains the nodes having the extremum values as well as the summation
over all nodes. This information may indicate whether a local or a global effect has been
detected.
If a default postprocessor has been defined, the topology data (item TOPO) together with
the rigid body modes are written completely in the appropriate format of the postprocessor. There they may be evaluated more detailed.
The default postprocessor may be defined using the DEFAULT command or the setting
may be included in the default definition file.

4. Contact analysis is performed automatically if contact conditions are defined. However,
contact analysis is not yet available in combination with the iterative solution scheme.
5. If a load history (i.e. $NLLOAD) is given the calulation is performed in the quasi-time
domain from TSTART to TEND, with the default values:
TSTART = min time from $NLLOAD and/or $NLRESULTS,
TEND = max. time from $NLRESULTS if existing, from $NLLOAD otherwise.
Note that the UCI parameter TSTART and TEND can only limit the time range of the
pre-defined load history from $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS respectively, i.e. it is not possible to add new additional time steps by this option.

Remarks:

TEMPERATURE command (PRECHECK, SYSTEM, etc.).
2. The preliminary check of the external loads is not complete since it does not contain the
contribution due to prescribed temperatures. Nevertheless, a raw checking is possible,
without computing the system matrices.

4. Temperature-dependent input data usually require a nonlinear analysis.
If a linear analysis is performed, temperature-dependent material data are evaluated at
the component temperature as defined by the system variant $PARAMETER COMPTEMP.
For temperature-dependent coefficients of convection, the nodal point temperature is assumed to be the component temperature.

indicate whether a local or a global effect has been detected.

Remarks:
1. The topology optimization is done in an own situation, referring to analyses which are to
be included in the optimization process.
2. The following analysis types may be referred by topology optimization:
• STATIC (see page 2-267 ff.)
• BUCKLING ANalysis (see page 2-106 ff.)
• INERTIA RELIEF (see page 2-197 ff.)
• VIBRATION ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.)

Contact analysis may be performed in STATIC and INERTIA RELIEF.
3. Element filling ratios are generated automatically and may be exported for each iteration
inside a TASK LOOP or for the final state after the TASK LOOP.
Nodal point filling ratios may be created using the GENerate NFRATIO command.
4. The step size for design variable changes may be manually controlled by using $DSVMLIM
(see page 3-991 ff.).
5. Allows to specify a minimum dimension size of the structure that will be approximately
targeted. Alternatively, a minimum dimension size canbe specified by using $DSVFILT
(see page 3-987 ff.) in the modification variant. Please refer to Example TOPO1 of
[um550] on page 15-6 ff.
6. Designed to handle a large number of “sparse” constraints together with a large number
of design variables, to fulfill maximum membersize conditions exactly. Requires the “AOS”
module.

Remarks:
1. System matrix generation is included in the command request. The command may be
terminated after the system matrix generation using the -SYSTEM- parameter. A continuation may be done by specifying the -MODES- (and further parameters) later on.
2. One of the parameters -MODES- or -FREQLIM- must be defined in any case. The limit
which is reached first terminates the analysis. The explicit definition of the number of
modes is computationally more efficient than the upper frequency limit hence if the number of modes is known it is recommended to use the -MODES- option exclusively. For
multilevel dynamic reduction (MLDR), however, the parameter FREQLIM must be specified in any case.
3. The accuracy given by the -ACCURACY- parameter is only valid for the first eigenvalue.
The relative accuracy decreases for higher frequencies until a minimum accuracy is
reached, which can be set by the default switch MINEVACC, DEFAULT see page 2-72.
4. Further parameters for the subspace iteration may be modified using the SET command
before starting the analysis:
• ADDVEC
• MAXBOX
• CHEBEXP
However, those parameters should be modified only with great care. Especially parameter
ADDVEC should only be increased if the frequency limit is used.

2-278

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

2.6 The EXEC section

VIBration ANalysis

5. By default the modes are normalized to the unit value for output purposes. To output the
original (stiffness orthonormalized) modes, use UCI command SET MODENORM = OFF.
6. Secondary results (e.g. stresses) are calculated from the internal representation of the
modes. In order to have consistent results in the output, switch MODENORM must be set
OFF.
7. Effective masses are computed for supported vibrations in order to have a measure for
the completeness of the modal model.

9. The vibration analysis is done with a shifted stiffness matrix: K ′ = K + α ∗ M . This
may be used to produce regular modes in case of a system with rigid body motions,
i.e. forcing a positive definite instead of a singular stiffness matrix. The resulting eigenvalues/frequencies are shifted back to the original un-shifted problem automatically (the
eigenmodes are not affected by the shift). However, note that the stiffness matrix K ′
obtained by this shift is not suited for parent situations in further dynamic analyses.
10. Multilevel dynamic reduction (MLDR) is based on an automatic decomposition of the active component into subcomponents and the solution of a dynamically (Craig-Bampton)
reduced substructure. The frequency limit for the condensation of subcomponents is
calculated as FREQLIM×MLDRBFAC respectively FREQLIM×MLDRFAC and the basic
component size is controlled by default switch MLDRSIZE. For a reduction of the interface
see default switch SUBGRED.
11. CONF = ORIG performs a back-transformation of the eigenvectors to the original component. Subsequent modal response analyses will be performed on the original component.
CONF = TOP performs no back-transformation. Subsequent modal response analyses
will be performed on the top component of the MLDR tree. This is the most efficient
option, if response results are required at a few locations only.
12. If external DOFs are present on top component level, the Craig-Bampton matrices are
provided automatically
13. A lower frequency limit is a very specific choice. Please ensure that this is a valid solution
for your dynamic system behavior. This option is only possible if the shift algorithm is
being used (see KSHIFT parameter).
14. If some eigenmodes seem to be rigid body modes, a rigid body mode update may be
done. Then the lowest eigenmodes are moved to the rigid body modes. See also the UCI
switches RBMCHECK and RBMUP_EDIST/RBMUP_RDIST.

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-279

UCI
EXEC

8. The computation of added mass effects requires the existence of a fluid model and interface elements to couple the fluid to the structure. The added mass effect is taken
into account only for the solution of the eigenvalue problem and the subsequent effective
mass computation, the structural mass matrix remains unchanged.

There are two independent types of weight analyses:
The elemental weight analysis computes mass, center of gravity and inertia tensor for each element. These are summed up
to obtain the total mass etc. of the model. Therefore only contributions of elements are taken into account (see remark 2 for
details).
The structural weight analysis is based on structural matrices
similar to the mass matrix. Therefore all contributions to the
mass are considered (see remark 5).
Select an element set for elemental weight analysis:
Use active element set (remark 3). If no active set is present,
the default set containing all elements of the appropriate degree of freedom type is used, e. g. ELEMDISP (see also
$ELEMENT).
In a loop over all (appropriate) element sets, mass and inertia
information is printed for each set (see remark 4).
Select degree of freedom type for elemental weight analysis:
Evaluate the weight of structural elements.
Evaluate the weight of fluid elements.
Select how much information is printed for structural weight
analysis:
Standard output only in the top component of the active configuration.
Extended output for all components (see remark 6 for details).

EXTENDED

WEIGHT [ANalysis]

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

Remarks:
1. Weight analysis computes model properties related to mass and inertia. The term ’weight’
does not refer to gravity here.

UCI
EXEC

2. The elemental weight analysis is based on a direct summation of element contributions.
Thus a direct matrix input is not taken into account and, for assembled components, only
the mass introduced by the elements of the actual component is taken into account.
It always uses a lumped mass approach (diagonal mass) – regardless of the
$PARAMETER MASS setting.
3. The elemental weight analysis may be performed also for a part of the structure by activating an element set previous to the weight analysis (see ACTIVE).
4. If SETS = ALL is chosen for the elemental weight analysis, all sets of one degree of
freedom type are evaluated for weight analysis consecutively. If a set name ends with
a different degree of freedom identifier as the currently active one, it is skipped (e. g.,
default extension is DISP, set name ends with TEMP).
5. The structural weight analysis is applicable at each component level, but is restricted to
DOFTYPE = DISP. As it is based on matrices, it is computational more expensive than
the elemental weight analysis and no element sets can be chosen. All contributions from
substructures, nonstructural mass ($NSTRMASS) and added fluid mass are taken into
account.
The structural weight analysis is based on consistent mass matrices, unless diagonal
mass is selected explicitly with the system block $PARAMETER MASS.
6. For the extended output option, condensed mass matrix BMMC and principal inertias
are printed in addition. Mass properties are output for each component of the active
configuration instead for the top component only.
Furthermore, the mass properties may be related to an arbitrary reference node by the
system block $PARAMETER REFNODE.
7. Please store the condensed and directional mass (BMMC, BMMCT, BMXRC and BMXRH)
for matrix models to obtain a correct structural weight output.
If the above books are not available, the structural weight analysis uses the condensed
mass matrix SMM as an approximation, which is incomplete if not all DOFs are external.
Please refer to example DEVX1V1 on page 8-15 ff. of [um550].
8. For models using dry condensation of fluid, the fluid mass is contained in the mass calculation once the solution step is performed. Please refer to example DEVX2V1 on page
8-34 ff. of [um550].
9. System mass matrix generation is included in the command request for both types.

Description:
The command derives new results R by modification of existing results X in a region of the
model defined by a node set. A function f (X) is applied to the original result values X. The
outcome is then multiplied by a scaling function s(c), which is a function of the column value
(time, frequency, load pattern id, etc.). The equation is as follows:
R = s(c) ∗ f (X)
where:
R
s(c)
f (X)
X

Is the derived result
Is the scaling factor, determined by the evaluation of a function s at the
current column value c (time, frequency, load pattern id)
Is the function applied to the original result values X
Is the original result

In case of complex arithmetic, a pair of functions must be given. The application of function fun r
to the complex result X gives the real part, which is subsequently multiplied with the scaling
function sr . The same holds for the functions fun i and si , which form the imaginary part of the
derived result R (see remark 2 and 3):
Re(R) = sr (c) ∗ fr (X)
Im(R) = si (c) ∗ fi (X)

Remarks:
1. The APPLY command is restricted to nodal point results. The value function f (X) is
applied individually to each component (i.e. DOF) of the original result X.
2. The first (sr ) and third (fun r ) function labels in the list create the real part of the new result
R, the second (si ) and fourth (fun i ) create the imaginary part. In case of real arithmetic,
only the labels sr and fun r may be given, si and fun i must be left blank.
3. In case of complex arithmetic, fun r and fun i should in general be functions of two variables. Otherwise only Re(X) will be used as input to the function.
4. The modification rule for the data is an overwrite rule, which keeps all initial data unchanged except the regions that are modified. The user is responsible for the definition of
unique sets. If a node is part of several sets, only the last modification rule will be applied.
5. In case of complex arithmetic the resulting book names are built from the name pattern
according to the following rules:
name
Denotes the amplitude data
nameF Stores the phase data
nameR Is the real part
nameI
Is the imaginary part of the result
6. The standard books associated with PERMAS items may not be changed in situ. User
books with user defined labels may be used in several subsequent APPLY commands,
allowing to split operations.
7. Within a task, the function application is performed for the active component only.
8. PERMAS functions are defined in the data input using e.g. $FUNCTION TABLE (see
page 3-1151 ff.)

prepared for a new computation. Nevertheless, the situation definition remains valid.
This means that the variants which build the situation are not changeable. But if several
analysis types may be performed within one situation (e.g. eigenvalue analysis and linear
static analysis) the situation may be used for a new computation.

5. The usage within task loops is not possible. Subsequent computations should be performed in separate tasks.

UCI

1. The definition of selection settings is valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be
done again since the valid selection range (usually) has changed.
2. A reduction of selection data may be defined in column direction using the appropriate
settings.
3. The selections are valid for the EVALUATION (see page 2-295 ff.) command and the
XYDATA (see page 2-327 ff.) selection with the COOR option.
4. Self-expanding field formats are also possible instead of fixed values.
5. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single selections or range selections. Up to 10 numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may be
specified.
COLUMNS = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
TIME = 1.,3. / 5. / 8.,10. selects time ranges 1. to 3., 5. to 5. and 8. to 10.

2.7 The SELECT section

EFREQMOD

Modify Eigenfrequencies

EFREQMOD

MODES

Type
I

Explanation
No. of modes requested for export.

Description:
The command may be applied after a VIBration ANalysis command and modifies mass and
stiffness matrices to shift eigenfrequencies according to the input given by a $EFREQMOD
data block. The modified data objects are intended to be exported to Excite.
Remarks:
1. The EFREQMOD command expects that in the vibration analysis all elastic eigenmodes
are calculated.
2. The eigenmodes requested by parameter MODES are orthonormalized with respect to
modified mass matrix; the sequence of modes, however, is kept. So the corresponding
eigenfrequencies may be no longer in ascending order.
3. The EFREQMOD command must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness
and mass matrices have to be reassembled internally before modification. Otherwise, the
FREQLIM parameter of the VIBration ANalysis command must be used.

2. The MAXMINTENSOR rule produces a result book, containing for each nodal point n, the
following 5 stress tensors σmax (n), σmin (n), σamp (n), σmean (n), and σrng (n). The tensors
are computed by the following procedure:
Denote by ρ(A) the spectral radius of a matrix A, i.e.
ρ(A) := max{|λ| : λ is eigenvalue of A}.
Then ρ(σ) is the principal stress with the largest absolute value. Furthermore let N denote the number of nodal points in the mesh, L the number of (selected) result columns
(loading patterns, time steps) and σ(n, l) the nodal point stress tensor of nodal point n for

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-299

UCI
SELECT

Parameter

EVALuation

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

the result column l. For each nodal point n, with 1 ≤ n ≤ N we compute for each pair of
result columns (i, j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ L


ρ σ(n, i) − σ(n, j)

and search at each node n the pair (i∗ , j ∗ ) for which ρ is maximal. This is the pair with
the largest stress difference. If there is no unique maximum, (i∗ , j ∗ ) will be the first pair
found having the maximum value.

The procedure yields the two tensors σ(n, i∗ ) and σ(n, j ∗ ). The tensor with the largest
principal stress (respecting the sign) is denoted by σmax (n), the remaining one is denoted
by σmin (n).
Using these two tensors, we define
the maximum amplitude stress tensor

UCI
SELECT

σamp (n) := (σmax (n) − σmin (n))/2,
the mean stress tensor
σmean (n) := (σmax (n) + σmin (n))/2,
and the range stress tensor
σrng (n) := σmax (n) − σmin (n).

Perform the generation of a surface/line mesh (hull) based on the given dimension of the selected elements.

PRETEST

Prepare a modal test by searching optimum sensor positions

PRETEST [LOOPS = loops]
[MACLIM = lim]
[DISTOL = tol]
[INCR = inc]
[ADDNODES = nset]

Type

Value

Explanation

LOOPS
MACLIM

I >0
0.0 < lim < 1.0

80
0.1

DISTOL

R > 0.0

1.0

0.0 < inc < 1.0
name

0.01

Maximum number of iterations to fulfill MAC criterion.
Maximum acceptable degradation of off-diagonal
MAC values (see remark 5).
Distance tolerance to find neighbors of “nominal” node
set (see remark 7).
Increment to reduce amplitude border (see remark 6).
Name of a node set that shall be part of the final node
set in any case.

INCR
ADDNODES

UCI
SELECT

Parameter

Description:
The command tries to find an appropriate set of nodes that are representative for the given
modal basis (X r ). The MAC criterion is applied to the reduced nodal basis
M AC =

(X tr X r )2
diag(X tr X r )diag(X tr X r )

in order to check the mode separation. If the desired maximum off-diagonal value is not reached
within the given number of iterations, the best state is selected automatically. Finally, two node
sets are prepared for further processing:
1. A minimum set, that may be used to restrict the modal displacements (see EXPORT,
PARAM). For this minimum set, a coarsening is being performed around the nodes with
extremum values to clearly identify the extremum.
2. An extended set (driven by DISTOL parameter) to get additional “neighbor” nodes, that
may be of interest for measurement positions. A corresponding element set may be
used to output a partial model. This extended set is always named as PRETEST. A
corresponding element set with the same name is also prepared in order to be able to
output a partial model (see remark to ITEM PART on page 2-390).
Of course, also all intermediate node sets are indicated and may be inspected manually. For
them, the EXPORT, CURRENT command may be used to restrict the displacement results,
after knowing the setname.

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-315

PRETEST

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

Remarks:
1. The command may only be used in conjunction with uncoupled solutions. Currently, only
VIBration ANalysis and FLuid VIBration ANalysis are supported.
2. A partial model may be used for the operation using the NSET option of the ACTIVE
command.
3. The mode normalization must be switched on by SET MODENORM = ON.
4. The function works only for modal solutions in the currently active component.

UCI
SELECT

5. The termination criterion is the sum of the MACLIM value and the highest off-diagonal
value of the full MAC matrix of the (partial) model. Note that even in the full MAC matrix
the off diagonal values will not be totally zero, because the eigenvectors are normalized
to X t KX = I and not to X t X = I.
6. The increment is used as a relative multiplier (scaled with the loop number) to select
additional extremum nodes within each level:
Rlim = Rmax − IN CR ∗ LOOP .
7. The distance is given in model units and has to be adapted by the user.
Example:
Please refer to example DEV6A of [um550].

SCALE

Scale a matrix

SCALE BOOK = name COEF = coef n1

Type

BOOK

name

COEF

R

Value

Explanation
Name of an existing input book to be scaled, see remark 1 on
page 2-317.
Scaling coefficient(s), see remark 2 on page 2-317.

Remarks:
1. The book is expected to be freedom oriented (internally partitioned). For nodal point
partitioned books see APPLY (see page 2-285 ff.) command.
2. If only 1 coefficient is given, all dofs of the matrix are scaled uniformly with this coefficient.
Otherwise, the coefficients must be given for each dof direction separately.
3. The global scaling of a matrix is a dangerous action. The presence of MPCs may lead to
undesirable results since the final matrix is a condensed one (only guiding dofs present).
The user is responsible to check the validity of this scaling approach.

1. The availability of sumload items is the same as for the GENERATE command. If not
already present, the secondary results will be generated within the command. Primary
quantities like loads are being created by a preceding command.
2. If NSET is specified, the node set must be an ordered set, that corresponds with its
dimension to the leading set bin. It contains the reference nodes for the load summary. If
omitted, the summary is related to the component system. If RSYS is given, the reference
direction is taken from the reference coordinate system.
3. RSYS defines the reference system for transformation. Can be supplied to NODE, NSET
or COG reference node. If neither NODE, NSET nor COG is specified, the reference
node is taken from RSYS (P 0) definition.
4. For the summation of nodal force quantities only NSETBIN is applicable.
5. For the summation of element energies or weights only ESETBIN is applicable.
6. For CUTTING FORCE, ESETBIN and NSETBIN are possible (as for the original CUTTING FORCE command option of the GENerate command).
7. For the calculation of cutting forces at a wetted surface in a fluid-structure coupled analysis, the fluid structure interface elements must be part of the element sets. Otherwise the
contribution of the fluid pressure will be missing.
8. The DOFTYPE option is mandatory for the computation of reaction forces. PRES is
currently not supported for cutting forces.
9. Displacement dependent loads, described by $LCMATRIX are currently only supported
by the INERTIA RELIEF command, that must precede the SUMLOAD command to create
the loads.
10. The computation of rigid body accelerations is based on structural weight analysis, that
has to be performed in advance.
11. The summation of relative quantities (i.e. densities) makes sense only, if the elements
are about the same size.
12. Item LOAD is only supported for DOFTYPE = DISP.

Remarks:
1. The extraction process is performed for the active node/element set of the active component. The set must be explicitly activated beforehand by the command ACTIVE (see
page 2-61 ff.).
2. For each item a default name for the xy-data pre-name exists (see section export (EXPORT
(see page 2-363 ff.)) for details.
3. The xy-data are not overwritten. If data for the same ITEM are extracted repeatedly, the
RESULT option must be used to create a new set of curves.

2-330

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

2.7 The SELECT section

XYDATA

4. For element results, the sequence of the data components is defined by the element
stress/force format as described in the element atlas (see chapter 4 ff.).
5. TYPE=REAL means the actual value for real results and the amplitude value for complex
results. For complex results, a pair of real / imaginary values may be extracted instead. If
the BOOK option is used, the label of the amplitude book must be specified in combination
with TYPE=COMPLEX.

7. RSYS=sysid selects a reference coordinate system for the COOR option. The meaning
of the coordinate values depends on the chosen reference system. The output of angles
is performed in degrees.
8. In case of RSYS=ROTB, nodal point results will be output in the ROTB system. This
renders a preceding TRANSform TO ROTB unnecessary.
If combined with option COOR, coordinates are sorted with respect to the component
system.
9. For complex arithmetics, the user may define a reference node, defining a reference
phase angle (for each selected dof). The amplitude value is then projected with the phase
difference of the selected node (and dof) to the reference node (/dof)
(R = A ∗ cos(φref − φ)).
I.e. the resulting real part of the quantity refers to the same state.
10. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single dcomp
selections or range selections. Up to 10 dcomp numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may
be specified.
DCOMP = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects dcomps 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
11. Result items which cannot be selected directly may be extracted by selecting a similar
item and then using the BOOK option with the appropriate label. See Appendix F for the
data object labels.

2.8 The PRINT section
Type

Value
-

NSET

name

∗
-

HISTORY

name

LOOP
ITERATION
PROGRESS
RESULTS

Explanation
Choose an existing element set to restrict the print of
data. This option overrules the ACTIVE setting.
Reset node set to default name (dependent on degree
of freedom type).
Choose an existing node set to restrict the print of
data. This option overrules the ACTIVE setting.
Optimization history / task loop data print settings, can
be set by the default switch HISTORY, DEFAULT see
page 2-70, see remark 6 on page 2-337:
Output of (history) data for task loops.
Output of (history) data for iterations, i.e. optimization
cycles.
Output of (history) data for progress steps, i.e. an improved design state.
Output of (history) data for results of subproblems, i.e.
a converged solution for multistart or Pareto.

Remarks:
1. The definition of output settings is valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be
done again since the valid selection range usually has changed.
2. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single selections or range selections. Up to 10 numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may be
specified.
COLUMNS = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
TIME = 1.0,3.0 / 5.0 / 8.0,10.0 selects time ranges 1.0 to 3.0, 5.0 to 5.0 and 8.0 to 10.0 .
3. Relative limit is supported for modal participation factor print only.
4. To print also lines which contain only zero values, use CURRENT BELOW = 0.0.
5. Self expanding field formats are also possible instead of fixed values. See appendix H for
further information.
6. To have a valid filtering, please perform any print after the optimization solution took place.
The filter works in two ways:
• For a task loop that doesn’t match the criterion, the print is completely switched off
(only for the current active task).
• For a matching task loop, the selected items are printed and the (optimization) xy
data are being filtered according to the criterion.

2.9 The EXPORT section
Type

HISTORY

name

Value

LOOP
ITERATION
PROGRESS
RESULTS

Explanation
Define the lower limit of values. (Absolute) Values below that limit are not exported. The meaning of the
input refers to the limit type, see remark 6 on page
2-369.
Optimization history/task loop data output settings,
can be set by the default switch HISTORY, DEFAULT
see page 2-70, see remark 8 on page 2-369.
Output of (history) data for task loops
Output of (history) data for iterations, i.e. optimization
cycles
Output of (history) data for progress steps, i.e. an improved design state
Output of (history) data for results of subproblems, i.e.
a converged solution for multistart, or pareto

Remarks:
1. The definition of output settings is valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be
done again since the valid selection range usually has changed.
2. A “,” as a separator defines a range selection, whereas a “/” separates either single selections or range selections. Up to 10 numbers, separated either by “,” or “/” may be
specified.
COLUMNS = 1,3 / 5 / 8,10 selects columns 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 and10.
TIME = 1.,3. / 5. / 8.,10. selects time ranges 1. to 3., 5. to 5. and 8. to 10.
3. The settings are valid for all selected items, therefore CURRENT must precede the ITEM
command.
4. A reduction of output data may be defined in row (node/element) and column (e.g. LPAT,
TIME) direction using the appropriate settings.
5. Corner node results are only supported for MEDINA. MEDINA is not able to handle fully
quadratic elements (e.g. HEXE27, PENTA18, QUAM9) with corner node results properly.
6. The BELOW filter is currently only applicable for modal participation factors.
7. Self-expanding field formats are also possible instead of fixed values.
8. To have a valid filtering, please perform any export after the optimization solution took
place. The filter works in two ways:
• For a task loop that doesn’t match the criterion, the output is switched off (only for
the current active task).
If no loop matches the criterion, or the output is done outside a task, the most recent
state is being exported in any case.

• For a matching task loop, the selected items are output and the (optimization) xydata are being filtered according to the criterion.
The export file counters correspond to the optimization cycle counter due to the
selected criterion.

Remarks:
1. If the command is specified without parameters, the export process is invoked to the
default postprocessor as described in the DEFAULT command (see page 2-66).

in chapter 7.1 ff.

matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.
5. The EXCITE export must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness and mass
matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.
6. The SIMDRIVE3D export must be executed in task mode, since the global stiffness and
mass matrices have to be reassembled internally, before invocation of the export process.

Specifies the pre-name part (at most 5 characters) for the xy descriptor and data sequences if
a non standard name is used.
Specifies a PARTSUM summation name
Specifies a book name different from the standard name of the item. See remark 18 on p.
2-390.
Request export of non-standard complex result
by specification of the name of the amplitude
book. See remark 18 on p. 2-390.

Remarks:
1. The range of supported items is postprocessor dependent. A detailed description may be
found in chapter 7.1 ff.
2. In contrast to the item command of the -PRINT- section, this command does not invoke
the output process. It is a pure selection command.
3. The item selections are valid only for the currently active situation and component. If a
change of the situation or the component is done, the selections have to be done again
since the selectable items (usually) have changed.
4. If the export commands are grouped within a task, an explicit selection of items may
be advantageous in order to double–check that all desired results have been computed
previously.
5. The creation of a combined model by ITEM TOPO COMBINE is performed in a loop upon
the whole configuration. Therefore it must not be called within a task. This option is
supported for PERMAS, PATRAN and IDEAS. For the numbering scheme of the combined model, please refer to the COMBNUM option of the DEFAULT (see page 2-66 ff.)
command.
6. ITEM TOPO COND builds a mathematical model description (only external DOFs) in
order to represent the substructure only by its coupling matrices.
7. ITEM TOPO DMODEL creates an artificial model for the verification of the design element
model topology. Design elements are exported as their finite element equivalent.
8. ITEM TOPO DESEARCHVOL generates an artificial model for postprocessing of the design element search volume. Design elements are exported as there FE element equivalent.
9. ITEM TOPO/MODL NEWCOOR selects nodal point coordinates modified by result values, depending on the analysis type. Default are displacement results, so a deformed
model will be written. In case of shape optimization, the coordinate positions of the actual

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

2-389

UCI
EXPORT

2.9 The EXPORT section

ITEM (DISP)

2 User Control Interface (UCI)

iteration are written (see example OP6 on page 14-85 ff. of [um550]).
If there are several result columns, a specific column (e.g. LPAT, TIME) must be selected
by the CURRENT command. With the BOOK option an alternative modification source
for the nodal coordinates can be choosen (see example BA3 on page 6-18 ff. of [um550]).
10. ITEM TOPO RADSURF selects the coarsened radiation surface (see $ELCOARSE) for
postprocessing purposes instead of the initial radiation mesh. See also example HT9 on
page 13-145 ff. of [um550].
11. The output of a partial model (ITEM PART) must be preceded by setting an element set
filter using the CURRENT ESET command. Additional nodes can be selected by using
the CURRENT NSET command also. A partial model with corresponding partial results
will be written.

UCI
EXPORT

12. ITEM HULL selects all elements that reside on the hull of the model, hence a reduction
is achieved mainly if solid elements are used. A partial model with corresponding hull
results will be written.
13. If the hull created by HGEN shall be output (e.g. after a topology or shape optimization),
ITEM TOPO SMOOTH is to be used.
14. ELEMENT COG must be explicitly requested and can be exported only to PERMAS.
15. Laminate stresses in the ply system are available only in PERMAS format. Element
stresses must have been calculated previously by the GENerate ELement STRESS command.
16. The weight summary item is only deselectable. It is exclusively available for the PERMAS
postprocessing format.
17. Modal accelerations, displacements and velocities must be explicitly selected for export.
18. With option BOOK, a non-standard result may be selected, e.g. created with the RESULT
option of a preceding UCI command. If the result is of complex arithmetic type and should
be exported as complex result, the option COMPLEX must be used instead. Here the
name of the amplitude book must be specified.
Example:
Please refer to example OP5V1 of [um550] for the use of ITEM COOR CHANGE and ITEM
MODL NEWCOOR.

Remarks:
