$MPC ISURFACE

3 Data Input (DAT)

5. If DPSYS = MATRIX is specified, then the coupling system is specified explicitly by its
base matrix.
6. If RELDOF is specified, then the additional degree of freedom identifier rdof is introduced
for each dependent node controlling the relative movement between dependent and guiding nodes in principal direction. This is realized by an additional part urel of an extended
constraint equation based on the first unit vector e1 of the local coupling system:
ud = Ag ug + urel ,

urel := urdof · e1 .

The degree of freedom identifier rdof may not be part of the activated degrees of freedom
at the dependent node to prevent undesired movement constraints. Typically rdof = 9 offers a secure separation. The movement actuation urdof must be given by a $PRESCRIBE
/ $PREVAL definition for rdof of the dependent node.

DAT
Constraints

7. For all nodes with dependent degrees of freedom, interpolation relations are determined
from guiding surface or surface set. The interpolation uses the normal projection of the
dependent nodes onto the interpolation (guiding) surface. If dependent nodes are not
located on the interpolation surface, for translational degrees of freedom node eccentricity
is taken into account by establishing a rigid lever arm connecting dependent node and
projected point in order to preserve overall balance of external loads and reactions.
8. If, for mechanical problems, the number of dependent dofs is chosen higher than the
number of dofs at the guiding nodes, the kinematic motion of the guiding nodes (volume
element(s)) is coupled with the dependent nodes (usually 6 degrees of freedom of the
shell element node) in the following way:
• The translational degrees of freedom are interpolated due to the shape function of
the guiding region.
• The rotational degrees of freedom of the dependent (shell) element nodes are interpolated by the translations of the guiding region.
See also page 3-340.
9. To control neighborhood relation determination between points and element surfaces, two
parameters are available: DISTOL and OUTTOL. A point may be aligned to an element
surface if its distance from the surface is less than DISTOL and its distance from the
boundary of the element is less than OUTTOL. If not input, the default values defined by
global system keys MPCDISTOL and MPCOUTTOL are used. See also figure F3-30
10. A table with statistical information on the neighborhood calculation of MPC ISURFACE
connections is printed in the result file.
11. For each node with dependent degrees of freedom a local coupling coordinate system
xC is used to establish interpolation relations from guiding surface or surface set.
If dependent nodes are not located on the interpolation surface, for translational degrees
of freedom node eccentricity is taken into account by establishing a rigid lever arm connecting dependent node and interpolation point in order to preserve overall balance of
external loads and reactions.

12. If DPSYS = NORMAL is specified, the calculation of the coupling coordinate system uses

The origin of the local coupling coordinate system is located at the position of the dependent node. The local surface normal direction at the position of the projection of this node
on the guiding surface geometry is used as first system axis xC . For the second and third
system axes fixing the tangential plane of the coupling, see remark 13.
13. For DPSYS = NORMAL a tangential direction can be specified using the YREF parameter, see figure F3-31.

Figure F3-31: Coupling coordinate system

The coupling normal axis xC is derived from the surface normal nS at each dependent
node’s nadir point N automatically (N is determined by the normal projection of the node
onto the guiding surface geometry). ** By the variable plane > 0 a reference plane
is selected from two of the three coordinate axes of the reference system rsys. For a
cylindrical or spherical reference system the reference plane is built by a local cartesian
system at the surface point according to the rules given on page 1-11. Parallel to this
reference plane an intersection plane is established cutting the surface at the point in
question, thus leading to a tangent line. The tangential vector ts is given by the vector
product nR × nS . The yC axis of the local coupling coordinate system is then calculated
by a rotation of ts about nS by angle γ. The third axis zC then completes this right-hand
system.

** See the $SURFACE input on on page 3-258pp for how the surface normal nS is defined.

Remarks:
1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.
2. The constraint conditions are always established between pairs of corresponding nodes.
3. If node sets are ordered, then node pairs are formed according to the sequence of nodes
in the sets. If node sets are not ordered, then node pairs are formed by assigning to each
node of the first set that node from the second set with the smallest distance. In any case,
both sets must contain the same number of nodes.
4. For MPC JOIN defined by node sets containing more than one node, the coupled node
pairs are listed in the result file.

Remarks:

$MPC NODE

3 Data Input (DAT)

The degree of freedom identifier rdof may not be part of the activated degrees of freedom
at the dependent node to prevent undesired movement constraints. Typically rdof = 9 offers a secure separation. The movement actuation urdof must be given by a $PRESCRIBE
/ $PREVAL definition for rdof of the dependent node.
7. Each guiding node has always up to three potential degrees of freedom and the dependent degrees of freedom are constrained to the translational movement (or temperatures
etc.) of the guiding node.
Degrees of freedom at the guiding node which are not coupled to the structure have to be
suppressed or prescribed.

DAT
Constraints

8. If DPITYP = NODE is specified, then the constraint conditions are established between
pairs of corresponding nodes. If the node sets are ordered, then node pairs are formed
according to the sequence of nodes in the sets. If node sets are not ordered, then node
pairs are formed by assigning to each node of the first set that node from the second
set with the smallest distance. In any case, both sets must contain the same number of
nodes.
9. If DPITYP = GROUND is specified, then homogeneous constraint conditions are established at the (dependent) nodes, i.e. declaring a prescribed/suppressed behavior which
requires at least one unconstrained degree of freedom. Thus the definition of DPDOFS =
1,2,3 is not supported.
10. If DPITYP = NODESAME is specified, then gid / gidset must consist of exactly one
guiding node.

The degree of freedom identifier rdof may not be part of the activated degrees of freedom
at the dependent node to prevent undesired movement constraints. Typically rdof = 9 offers a secure separation. The movement actuation urdof must be given by a $PRESCRIBE

to be suppressed or prescribed.
• The constraints for T and ∆T are separated; there is no coupling between them.

$MPC WLSCON

3 Data Input (DAT)

Weighted Averaged Connection
The displacements associated with the dependent degrees of freedom ddof at node did are
constrained to a rigid body movement defined by the averaged, weighted displacements of the
guiding degrees of freedom gdof at nodes gid or gidset, respectively.
If the constraint is defined for temperature degrees of freedom, then the dependent temperature
is defined by the averaged, weighted temperature at the guiding nodes.

Remarks:
1. Please refer to the global MPC remarks which are valid for all MPC types.
2. Weighted averaged connections are restricted to displacement or temperature degrees
of freedom.

4. If displacement degrees of freedom are constrained:
• The sum of all guiding degrees of freedom must be capable to describe an arbitrary
kinematic motion of a rigid body, i.e. at the dependent point all six degrees of freedom must be provisionally supported by the WLSCON – even if not all of them are
taken as dependent DOFs !
• The displacements at the guiding degrees of freedom are weighted by factor w and
all guiding contributions are averaged by least square method to define the motion
of a rigid body. The dependent degrees of freedom are constrained to that rigid body
motion.
• If gdof is omitted, all translational or all translational and rotational degrees of freedom of the corresponding node gid are assumed to be guiding degrees of freedom.
See also switch MPCWLSGDOF, SET/SHOW see page 2-41
• Degrees of freedom at the guiding nodes which are not coupled to the structure have
to be suppressed or prescribed.
• It is not recommended to use rotational degrees of freedom as guiding degrees of
freedom except if necessary regarding paragraph one (e.g. if the guiding nodes are
collinear).
• Rotated node bases are taken into account automatically, i.e. the displacements of
the guiding nodes with (possibly rotated) local bases are transformed to the component system before calculating the rigid body movement.
5. If temperature degrees of freedom are constrained:
• If gdof is omitted, always two degrees of freedom of the corresponding node gid are
assumed to be guiding degrees of freedom.
• Degrees of freedom at the guiding nodes which are not coupled to the structure (e.g.
∆T at solids) have to be suppressed or prescribed.
• The constraints for T and ∆T are separated; there is no coupling between them.
6. If w is omitted, w = 1.0 is assumed.
7. See also default switch WLSSCALE, DEFAULT see page 2-81

Remarks:
1. For specification of MPC names see remark 1 on page 3-126.
2. The definition of update rules for multipoint constraints is only possible within the constraint variant of a single or top component.
3. For the update rules to be applied the update policy has to be set to MANUAL via the
default switch (MPCUPDATE, DEFAULT see page 2-73). The MANUAL update includes
an update of the constraints neighborhood relation if applicable like for e.g. for $MPC
ISURFACE. In contrast, the automatic update does not update neighborhood relations.
4. The update of multipoint constraints is restricted to geometric nonlinear analyses, see
NLMATERIAL and DIRECT NLTIME.
5. The update of multipoint constraints is only available for the following types:
• RIGID, see $MPC RIGID,
• WLSCON, see $MPC WLSCON,
• RIGCON, see $MPC RIGCON and
• WLSSURFACE, see $MPC WLSSURFACE.
The update of interpolation region constraints of the types
• ISURFACE, see $MPC ISURFACE,
• ILINE, see $MPC ILINE and
• IVOLUME, see $MPC IVOLUME
is also available, but cannot be activated with parameter TYPE (also not with TYPE =
ALL). The update of these types must be requested by a separate $MPCUPDATE without
any TYPE specification and the label mpc in the data line.
6. Parameter NODES selects the nodes of the multipoint constraint definition to be updated.
If NODES = GUIDING is specified, only the coordinates of the nodes with guiding degrees of freedom are updated for the calculation of the modified constraint equations.

8. If a node is affected by multiple constraints, then its coordinates must be updated either
via all or none of these constraints.

DAT

rsys

Explanation

Nodal point identifier.
Node set name.
Identifier of node i.
Coordinates of node i, referring to system rsys. Meaning depends on kind
of reference system. Angles must be input in degrees.
Cartesian system:
x y z
Cyl/Conical/Helix/Thread: r ϕ z
Standard Spherical rsys: r ϑ ϕ (polar ϑ as 2nd coordinate)
Geo-Spherical/Toroidal:
r ϕ ϑ
Label (integer, name or text string) of reference system for given coordiI≥0
name/text nates. A zero rsys (default) refers to the component system.

Remarks:
1. If parameter RSYS or EULER is present on the $ROTB line, the indicated reference
system is used to establish the rotated node bases. Reference systems are defined by
data blocks $RSYS, see page 3-241ff. and figure F3-32 on following page. For cylindrical
or spherical reference systems the local cartesian system for the orientation of the node
basis is generated using the generation rules defined on page 1-11.
2. If Euler rotations are present then the given rotations are applied as consecutive intrinsic
rotations to the axes of the rotated node basis derived from rsys in the sequence specified (consecutive intrinsic rotations means that the 2nd / 3rd rotation is based on the new
current axes derived from the 1st / 2nd rotation). Up to 3 rotations may be specified (same
axis may be used for 1st and 3rd rotation).
3. If parameter RSYS and EULER are omitted, the local cartesian system for the orientation
of the rotated node basis is established using three points according to rule valid to establish a cartesian reference system, see page 1-11. Each point may be given by a node
number or by its coordinates.
4. The coordinates of points may be given in the component system (default) or in any other
reference system rsys, which may be a cartesian, cylindrical or spherical one.
5. Rotated node bases defined within the constraint variant bracket are valid only within
current constraint variant. If rotated node bases should be the same for all constraint
variants it is recommended to define them using the $ROTB data block within the structure
definition bracket, see page 3-236.
6. If a nodal point carries external degrees of freedom, the rotated node basis must be
defined in the structure definition bracket.
7. A rotated basis may not be defined for a hypercomponent node, which is defined via
subcomponent coincidences (inserted via $SUBCOMP). The local system of this node
must be defined in the subcomponent directly.

$ADDMATRIX

3 Data Input (DAT)

5. The geometric stiffness used in buckling analysis is included automatically and must not
be requested by $ADDMATRIX.
6. For nonlinear analysis no additional matrices may be requested.
7. For the dynamic analysis of rotating structures referring to the co-rotating frame of reference, geometric stiffness, centrifugal stiffness and Coriolis matrix are needed. However,
centrifugal stiffness as well as Coriolis matrix may be requested only if the geometric
stiffness is included.
8. For the dynamic analysis of rotating structures referring to the inertial frame for reference,
geometric stiffness, convective stiffness and gyroscopic matrix are needed. However,
convective stiffness as well as gyroscopic matrix may be requested only if the geometric
stiffness is included. Furthermore, the rotating part must be axisymmetric.

Remarks:
1. Definition of static mode shapes to be added to the set of eigenvectors is possible only
within a system variant of a single or top component (for an exception see remark 13),
and is taken into account only in child situations for the transformation to modal space.
2. Additional static mode shapes are available for analyses in modal space based on mechanical (VIBRATION ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.)), fluid (FLUID VIBration ANalysis (see
page 2-144 ff.)) or coupled fluid-structure (FSCOUPLED VIBration ANalysis (see page
2-147 ff.)) eigenvalue analysis.
3. In coupled fluid-structure analyses, additional static mode shapes may be specified for
displacement as well as for pressure degrees of freedom.
4. If SOURCE = INPUT is specified, each data block defines one additional static mode
shape. If SOURCE = LOAD or SOURCE = RESULT is specified, each data line defines
one additional mode shape (for LPAT = ALL one for each load pattern). If SOURCE
= ELEMENTS is specified, one additional mode shape per each natural deformation of
each element is generated.

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-397

$ADDMODES

3 Data Input (DAT)

5. Non-standard degrees of freedom of linear control elements (e.g. CONTRL5 on page
4-488 ff.) must not be used to define static mode shapes; they are included automatically.
6. If SOURCE = INPUT (default) is specified, the following rules are valid:
• In list(dof ) the nodal point degrees of freedom are specified; list(x) contains the
corresponding nodal point values.
• If list(dof ) is omitted then the sequence of nodal point values must correspond with
the sequence of degrees of freedom, starting with 1. Trailing zeroes may be omitted.
• Depending on dof type the nodal point values are displacements, pressures etc.
• Shape values for rotational degrees of freedom are expected to be given in radians.

DAT
System

• Input of shape values is not possible for degrees of freedom which are declared as
suppressed, prescribed or external, or used as dependent degrees of freedom im
MPC’s.
• Input data may refer to a reference system given by parameter RSYS. If parameter
RSYS is omitted, components of displacements etc. are referring to the (possibly rotated) local node coordinate system, RSYS = 0 means referring to component
system. If the reference system rsys is a cylindrical or spherical one then input data
refer to a local cartesian system which is generated according to the generation rules
defined on page 1-11.
7. If SOURCE = LOAD is specified, additional mode shapes are calculated as static deflections under the loads defined in the corresponding loading variant, one mode shape per
specified load pattern. By LPAT = ALL all load patterns are specified. In any case, each
load pattern may be specified only once.
8. If SOURCE = LOAD is specified in a collector situation where loading variants of different
situations are assembled (see $SITUATION, parameter ASSEMBLY), then LPAT = ALL
refers to all load patterns of all collected situations. If, however, LPAT = patid is specified,
the load pattern patid must exist in all collected situations.
9. If SOURCE = RESULTS is specified, results of other situations are used as additional
mode shapes. No result vector may be specified twice. If no selection is specified,
COLUMN = LAST, i.e. last column of result book is assumed.
10. If SOURCE = ELEMENTS is specified, for each natural force (e.g. generalized force belonging to elongation) of each specified element an additional static mode shape is generated. This option, however, is restricted to spring, damper and control elements:

3-398

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

3.2 Model Data

$ADDMODES

SPRING6
SPRINGX3

DAMP6

CONTRL10

11. If real eigenvalues are calculated with the MLDR-option (see UCI-command VIBRATION
ANalysis (see page 2-276 ff.)), then the results must be transformed to origin component,
i.e. the default CONF = ORIG must be used.
12. If additional static mode shapes are requested in a modal coupled fluid-structure analysis, eigenvalue calculation without mass (by NOMASS = YES) or without compressibility
(by NOCOMPR = YES) are not possible (see UCI command FSCOUPLED VIBration
ANalysis (see page 2-147 ff.)). The same is true for approximation or neglecting singular
coupling term by SCTAPP > 0.
13. Additional static mode shapes by SOURCE = ELEMENTS may be requested in subcomponents. The degrees of freedom at the nodes of the corresponding elements, however,
must be external ones in all components up to the top component if not suppressed.
14. For mixed boundary static condensation the actual rigid body modes of the reference situation are used to compute the inertia relief attachment modes. The modes must be
requested in the reference situation used in the definition of $EXTERNAL MODEs. The
modes are only available if the reference situation has rigid body modes.
If requested in another analysis, the geometric rigid body modes for the free component
are used to compute the load vectors for the inertia relief attachment modes.
15. Modal damping by $MODDAMP may be specified for static mode shapes too (with the
exception of modes defined by element deformations), but, however, the final sequence
of modes is not known until the transformation to modal space is done.

Remarks:
1. Overall damping may be defined for any top, single or subcomponent. In addition, it may
also be specified in system variants of child situations where data from another system
variant are inserted, see $INSERT VARIANT.
2. Overall damping may be used for any kind of dynamic analysis where damping may be
applied (including fluid-structure-coupled analysis) but not for modal spectral response
analysis, see MODAL SPECTRAL ANalysis (see page 2-234 ff.).
3. If overall damping is defined in a subcomponent, the complete reduced stiffness or mass
matrix is taken into account, i.e. Guyan as well as Craig-Bampton parts. Furthermore, no
component above in the configuration may contain the same type of overall damping.
4. If overall damping is defined in a single or top component, then the corresponding damping matrix in modal space is diagonal.
5. Rayleigh (proportional) damping leads to the viscous damping matrix
D = αK + βM

with the constant values α and β, the stiffness matrix K and the mass matrix M . If for a
component both Rayleigh coefficients should be defined, then they have to be input within
the same data block.
6. Overall structural damping yields a complex stiffness matrix of the form
K̄ = (1 + igC (f ))K
with damping factor

frequency-dependent function, see $FUNCTION. If the function identifier is omitted, the
function is replaced by the constant value 1.0 .

Remarks:
1. Initial values and admissible discrete values for design variables may be defined only in
system variants of single or top components.
2. Initial values of design variables must be greater than zero, except for design variables
used for coordinate modifications, by $DSVNODE and $DVCOOR, if an OPTIM command
is executed.
3. Initial values are ignored for design variables, which are dependent due to design variable
linking.
4. If design variables are specified as basic variables by $BASVAR, initial values are defined
by mean values (expectation) of the corresponding probability distribution functions, and
must not be input directly.
5. If for an geometrical property design variable no initial value is defined, then the initial
value for optimization is calculated from original properties and property to design variable
relation. This is, however, only possible for direct relations and must be without any
contradiction, see page 3-410 for further details.

DAT
System

1. Design variable to design node coordinate relations may be defined only in system variants of single or top components.
2. The direction of coordinate modification is specified by the coordinate identifier idcoor,
which may refer to component system (default), a reference system rsys (see remark 3)
or to a surface surf (see remark 4).
3. If the reference system rsys is a cylindrical or spherical one, then the coordinates refer to
a local cartesian system which is generated according to the generation rules defined on
page 1-11.
4. If the coordinate refers to a surface, the design node must belong to the surface. The
x-axis matches the surface normal at the design node as specified in the $SURFACE
definition. Only for nodes on the surface boundary additionally y- and z-axes are available.
These directions are coplanar to the surface tangent plane and approximate the normal
and tangent to the boundary, see figure F3-33.

• Reference systems and surface normals are not updated even if nodal points used

Remarks:

2. All design variables dsvid referenced within one Geometrical Data Record must be assigned to the same design element deid. The defined relations are then valid for all elements with the specified Geometrical Data Record and assigned to that particular design
element. Elements with different Geometrical Data Records or elements not assigned to
that design element are not concerned.
3. Geometrical Data Records contain named parts called fields, see $GEODAT data block
description, where each field contains a list of geometrical data. Within a field f ield,
one particular item can be identified by its index. Consequently, the dependency of geometrical data on design variables is inputted referring to field name f ield and index ind.
Repeated fields may be distinguished using the field repetition counter rep.
4. For direct dependencies there is only one design variable per data line, for functional
dependencies one tuple with n items where n is the number of independent variables
of the corresponding function. All design variables must be valid for the whole design
element.
5. To relate design variables and properties, the following reference values X are used:
• If a design variable is valid for the whole design element then the reference value X
is given by the design variable value itself

Remarks:

2. The defined relations are valid for all elements with the referenced material and belonging
to any design element the referenced design variables are assigned to. Elements with
different materials or elements not assigned to those design elements are not concerned.
3. A material property datum is referenced by the material property name prname (e.g.
ELASTIC) and its index in the sequence of input data for that property. The sequence
of input data, however, depends on material type (e.g. GENERAL) and on the degree
of anisotropy of the material, therefore the index of a datum refers always to the input
sequence actually done for the referenced property.
4. If the basic material property datum is not constant but depends on physical quantities
like temperature etc., then the constant factor c in the relation between property value and
design variables (see below) may be replaced by a function c(y) where vector y contains
the state variables (e.g. temperature or time) the material property value depends on. The
dependencies must be specified by paramater DEP on the header line, and the sequence
of dependency specification determines the sequence of independent variables (state
variables) of the function c(y).
5. In the current implementation, frequency dependent damping is not supported.

DAT

2. A design variable to system parameter relation may be restricted to a region, set etc. by

3. If KIND = DIRECT is specified, a linear relationship exists between design variable x and
the value P of the parameter in question. So it holds
P (i) = C x(i)

with

C=

P (0)
x(0)

If P (0) = 0, the initial value of the design variable x(0) must be equal zero and vice versa,

(i)

P (i) = fun(xj , j = 1, m)
For function definition see $FUNCTION data block description, pages 3-1112 ff..
Initial values of the corresponding design variables cannot be calculated for general function dependency but must be defined within a $DSVVAL data block. Furthermore, the
parameter value for the first optimization step is calculated according to the given function without reference to the original parameter value.
5. Initial values of the design variables may be calculated if KIND = DIRECT is specified.
The initial value is then calculated as the mean value of all system parameters dependent
on that design variable. For details see below.

Explanation
Real part is selected.
Imaginary part is selected. Only possible for complex loads / results.
Name of element set to restrict definition to.

Remarks:

2. KIND = PRIMARY means the standard load-dependent system matrices for all linear
analyses. Only for geometrical stiffness matrices it holds:
• In linear buckling analyses (see BUCKling ANalysis) the primary geometrical stiffness matrix forms the second matrix of the eigenvalue problem.
• In rotational speed dependent analyses (see e.g. MODAL ROTATING etc.) the primary geometrical stiffness matrix is proportional to Ω2 and varies with the rotational
speed.
• In all other linear analyses the primary geometrical stiffness matrix is simply added
to the elastic stiffness matrix.
3. With KIND = KEEP it is possible to specifiy an additional geometrical stiffness matrix in
linear analyses which is kept constant in any case, i.e.:
• In linear buckling analyses (see BUCKling ANalysis) this geometrical stiffness part
is added to the elastic stiffness matrix.
• In rotational speed dependent analyses (see e.g. MODAL ROTATING etc.) this geometrical stiffness part is added to the elastic stiffness matrix and must not depend
on rotational speed. The results must be referenced on the data line by a static load
pattern with LPAT = patid or by TIME = {t | LAST} for a static load history specified
by a $NLLOAD data block.
• In all other linear analyses that geometrical stiffness matrix part is simply added to
the elastic stiffness matrix.
4. No other load-dependent system matrices may be established by an $ELSTATE LOAD
data block with KIND = KEEP. Furthermore, if an additional geometrical stiffness matrix
should be established, a primary geometrical stiffness matrix must be requested in any
case.
5. Constant element load state values are specified by reference to the loads / results of a
foreign situation and are only available within a system variant of single or top components
referring to another system variant by a $INSERT VARIANT data block. The situation
reference is valid for whole configuration, and the referred situation must contain the
system variant inserted into the current variant.

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-431

DAT
System

1. Constant element load state values are used to generate constant load-dependent system matrices in linear analysis, e.g. geometrical stiffness matrices, see data block
$ADDMATRIX.

$ELSTATE LOAD

3 Data Input (DAT)

6. Each situation, to which a system variant with constant load state definition is assigned,
must have the same constraint variant, i.e. it must contain the constraint variant of that
foreign situation the constant load state belongs to.
7. To execute a situation with system matrices depending on constant element load state
values, the complete primary results of the foreign situation must be available.
8. According to the data line one column of the results of the specified situation is selected.
If loading is expected (e.g. centrifugal stiffness), the corresponding load is extracted. If
element stress state is expected (e.g. geometrical stiffness), the corresponding element
stresses are evaluated.
9. The load state definition must be unique, i.e. only one load / result specification is possible
within one system variant.

Remarks:
1. Element state variable values describe the internal state of elements, and may be used
e.g. for evaluation of material data to establish system matrices. They may not be given
implicitly as results of the actual analysis.
2. Element state variable values may be input for elements, at structural nodes or may be
given by a scalar field, i.e. by a function. Furthermore, they may be given by reference to
a foreign situation.
3. The specification of additional element state variable values must be unique, i.e. for each
type of element state variable only one specification per element is possible.
4. If additional element state variable values are defined at structural nodes, then the value
for each element is calculated as arithmetical mean of the values at element nodes. To

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-435

DAT
System

h

$ELSTATE POROSITY

3 Data Input (DAT)

do so, only elements are taken into accout where all nodes of the element are provided
with the additional element state variable, other elements are ignored. Internal element
nodes are always ignored in that process.
5. For additional element state variable values defined at structural nodes an element set
may be specified. Then, in a first step, all input definitions without element set, if any,
are processed to determine loaded elements according to the rule given in remark 4. In
the following steps all input definitions belonging to the same element set are collected
and processed, delivering further loaded elements. Nodes with different element set
specifications are not mixed to determine loaded elements.

DAT
System

6. If additional element state variable values are specified by a scalar field, then that field
must be given by a function in 3D space. The value for each element is then calculated
by evaluation of the function at the element center which is calculated as mean of the
element corner node coordinates.
The calculation is done for the original node coordinates and is not updated if the coordinates are modified by the solution (.e.g. during optimization).
7. If for the element state variable definition by function a reference system label unequal
zero is specified, then the coordinates of the element center are transformed to the reference system, and the function evaluation is done for the transfomed coordinates.
8. If the field specification by function is done without reference to an element set, then it is
valid for the whole component.
9. Additional element state variable values may be specified by reference to the results of a
foreign situation. This option is only available in single or top components. If no element
set is specified, then the specification is valid for the whole configuration.
10. To access additional element state variable values from a foreign situation, that situation
must be scanned or executed already, depending on the type of state variable.
11. According to the data line one column of the data / results of the specified situation is
selected.
12. If for an element the additional element state variable is not specified, the default value, if
any, is used.
Example:
$ELSTATE POROSITY ITYPE = ELEMENTS
Lower_Cord 0.25
$ELSTATE POROSITY ITYPE = NODES
Upper_Cord_Nodes Upper_Cord 0.30

5. If additional element state variable values are defined at structural nodes, then the value

Remarks:
1. Element temperature state values are used to access temperature-dependent material
data in analysis types without temperature degrees of freedom, and may be specified for
all elements able to carry temperature degrees of freedom. They are, however, not used
for the (optionally load-dependent) thermal expansion coefficients.
2. Temperature-dependent data describing elastic material behavior are evaluated at an element mean temperature.
3. Element temperature state values may be specified directly at elements or at structural
nodes (SOURCE = INPUT), by reference to a load pattern or load history of the corresponding loading variant (SOURCE = LOAD / NLLOAD) or by reference to the results of
a specified situation (SOURCE = RESULTS) of a heat transfer analysis. Reference to a
situation is only possible within a system variant of a single or top component and is valid
for the whole configuration.
4. The element temperatures referred by SOURCE = INPUT / LOAD / RESULTS define a
constant temperature state whereas SOURCE = NLLOAD defines a time dependent
temperature state that may lead to non-constant system matrices accordingly, see remark 6.
5. Also note that SOURCE = NLLOAD needs the NLS license key for nonlinear material behaviour and is applicable with static analyses only (e.g. STATIC, INERTIA, NLMATERIAL,
NLINERTIA).

3-442

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

V 19.00.287

3.2 Model Data

$ELSTATE TEMP

6. For a nonlinear static analysis (command NLMATERIAL or NLINERTIA) only
SOURCE = NLLOAD is possible.
7. The temperature definition must be unique, i.e. only one result specification or one load
pattern selection or one direct input per element or per structural node is possible within
one system variant but no combination of the three source types.
8. If temperatures are defined at nodes (by results / load pattern or directly by input), the
mean value for each element is calculated as arithmetical mean of the temperature value
at the element nodes.

10. For elements or nodes, respectively, where no temperature is specified, the reference
temperature defined by $PARAMETER COMPTEMP is used as default temperature.
11. In list(dof ) the nodal point temperature degrees of freedom are specified; list(x) contains
the corresponding temperature values. Although input for all nodal point temperature
degrees of freedom is possible, only the node temperature (1st degree of freedom) is
used to evaluate element mean temperature.
12. If list(dof ) is omitted then the sequence of temperature values must correspond with the
sequence of degrees of freedom, starting with 1. Trailing zeroes may be omitted.
13. For SOURCE = LOAD and SOURCE = NLLOAD the element mean temperatures are
derived from the element node temperatures defined as thermal loads via load types
TEMP, TEMPDIFF and TEMPGRAD for the specified static load pattern patid or for the
load patterns referred by the load history $NLLOAD, respectively. For nodes where no
thermal loads are given the default temperature, is assumed, see remark 10.
14. For SOURCE = NLLOAD the element temperature state is computed as follows:
P
STATIC:
Tel (t) = Tcomp +
si (t) · (Ti − Tcomp )
P
NLMATERIAL:
(A) Tel (t) = Tcomp or
si (t) · Ti
if Ti exists
P
(R) Tel (t) = Tcomp or
si (t) · (Ti − T0 ) if Ti −T0 exists
Tcomp is the default element reference temperature set by system variant $PARAMETER
COMPTEMP. For NLMATERIAL, (A) and (R) denote default parameter NLSCALETEMP
set to ABSTEMP / RELTEMP, respectively. T0 is the reference temperature with zero thermal expansion, see loading variant $PARAMETER REFTEMP or $REFVAL TEMP, respectively.
15. For SOURCE = RESULTS the element mean temperatures are derived from the resulting
temperature distribution of a thermal analysis performed within another situation. If no further selection is specified, COLUMN = LAST, i.e. last column of result book is assumed.

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-443

DAT
System

9. If for an element the mean value is specified directly, it takes precedence over the mean
value calculated from directly inputted nodal point values.

given by a scalar field, i.e. by a function. Furthermore, they may be given by reference to
a foreign situation.
3. The specification of additional element state variable values must be unique, i.e. for each
type of element state variable only one specification per element is possible.
4. If additional element state variable values are defined at structural nodes, then the value
for each element is calculated as arithmetical mean of the values at element nodes. To

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-447

DAT
System

h

$ELSTATE VOLFFRAC

3 Data Input (DAT)

do so, only elements are taken into account where all nodes of the element are provided
with the additional element state variable, other elements are ignored. Internal element
nodes are always ignored in that process.
5. For additional element state variable values defined at structural nodes an element set
may be specified. Then, in a first step, all input definitions without element set, if any,
are processed to determine loaded elements according to the rule given in remark 4. In
the following steps all input definitions belonging to the same element set are collected
and processed, delivering further loaded elements. Nodes with different element set
specifications are not mixed to determine loaded elements.

DAT
System

6. If additional element state variable values are specified by a scalar field, then that field
must be given by a function in 3D space. The value for each element is then calculated
by evaluation of the function at the element center which is calculated as mean of the
element corner node coordinates.
The calculation is done for the original node coordinates and is not updated if the coordinates are modified by the solution (.e.g. during optimization).
7. If for the element state variable definition by function a reference system label unequal
zero is specified, then the coordinates of the element center are transformed to the reference system, and the function evaluation is done for the transfomed coordinates.
8. If the field specification by function is done without reference to an element set, then it is
valid for the whole component.
9. Additional element state variable values may be specified by reference to the results of a
foreign situation. This option is only available in single or top components. If no element
set is specified, then the specification is valid for the whole configuration.
10. To access additional element state variable values from a foreign situation, that situation
must be scanned or executed already, depending on the type of state variable.
11. According to the data line one column of the data / results of the specified situation is
selected.
12. If for an element the additional element state variable is not specified, the default value, if
any, is used.
Example:
$ELSTATE VOLFFRAC ITYPE = ELEMENTS
Lower_Cord 0.25
$ELSTATE VOLFFRAC ITYPE = NODES
Upper_Cord_Nodes Upper_Cord 0.30

Remarks:
1. Element system definitions which are inputted by $ELSYS within the $SYSTEM bracket,
are inserted into the geometrical data records of the referenced elements in the actual
system variant, see $GEODAT.

DAT
System

2. The definition of local element systems is possible only if the geometrical data record of
each referenced element contains the field PREF, REFSYS or REFSYSX resp., or for
gasket elements, see remark 3. With the exception of POINT and RSYS, the specification made on header line must match the field in the geometrical data record of each
referenced element. For that, and for the rules to establish the local element system see
element description.
3. For gasket elements, the definition of element systems with option POINTS or RSYS is
optional, and must be done within the $STRUCTURE bracket.
4. Local element systems which may be defined via REFSYS or REFSYSX resp. can be established by three points (or two points resp.), see pictures below, using the specification
POINTS, or can be derived from a reference system, see remark 6, if RSYS is specified.
5. Beam element systems are established using a reference point PREF. This reference
point may be determined with reference to a system defined by three points, using the
specification POINTS, see picture below, or to a reference system, see remark 6, if RSYS
is specified. In any case, the direction from the center of gravity of the first beam section
to the reference point is given by the direction of the first coordinate axis of the reference
system (local cartesian system for cylindrical or spherical reference system).
6. If RSYS is specified on header line, the given reference system rsys is used to establish the local element system. Reference systems are defined by data blocks $RSYS or
$RSYSAX for axisymmetric structures, respectively. RSYS = 0 means component system.
For cylindrical or spherical reference systems the local cartesian system for the orientation of the element local system is generated using the generation rules defined on page
1-11.
If parameter AXES is omitted, the local element system coincides with the local cartesian
system, else idof x specifies the axis of the local cartesian system which is used as x-axis
of the element system, and idof y specifies the axis of the local cartesian system which
is used as y-axis of the element system. Following values may be used:
1
(-1) : Positive (negative) x-axis of reference system (r-axis for axisymmetric structures).
2
(-2) : Positive (negative) y-axis of reference system (z-axis for axisymmetric struc-

Temperature, time, space

DAT
System

5. The convective film coefficient may depend on temperature, time and space. It is calculated at node i according to
Formula
α = α0
α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i )
α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i , t)
α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i , t, xi , yi , zi )

where Ti is the nodal point temperature and TF,i the corresponding temperature of the
surrounding fluid, t is the actual time in transient analysis and xi , yi , zi are the cartesian
coordinates of node i referring to component system. The surrounding temperatures TF,i
must be input within the corresponding loading variant, see $DISLOAD TEMPFILM, page
3-663 and $DISLOADN TEMPFILM, page 3-740.
6. The convective film coefficient function can be defined as general temperature-dependent
function with two, three or six independent variables, see $FUNCTION, page 3-1112 ff.,
for the meaning of the independent variables see remark 5.
7. Temperature-dependent input data usually require a nonlinear analysis.
If a linear analysis is performed, the nodal point temperature Ti is assumed to be the
component temperature as defined by the system variant $PARAMETER COMPTEMP.
8. If the function identifier fun is omitted or equal zero the function is replaced by the constant
value 1.0, leading to a constant convective film coefficient α = α0 .
9. Input of emissivity ε0 = 0 represents a totally reflecting surface, i.e. the corresponding
element surface is included in the heat radiation analysis.
10. If surrounding temperatures for radiation are needed, they may be input within the corresponding loading variant, see $DISLOAD TEMPINF, page 3-669 and $DISLOADN
TEMPFINF, page 3-744, or fixed by loading variant parameter TEMPINFTY, see 3-852.

where node 7 is the fourth corner node and node 9 the third one.

α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i )
α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i , t)
α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i , t, xi , yi , zi )

where Ti is the nodal point temperature and TF,i the corresponding temperature of the
surrounding fluid, t is the actual time in transient analysis and xi , yi , zi are the cartesian
coordinates of node i referring to component system. The surrounding temperatures TF,i
must be input within the corresponding loading variant, see $DISLOAD TEMPFILM, page
3-663 and $DISLOADN TEMPFILM, page 3-740.
6. The convective film coefficient function can be defined as general temperature-dependent
function with two, three or six independent variables, see $FUNCTION, page 3-1112 ff.,
for the meaning of the independent variables see remark 5.
7. Temperature-dependent input data usually require a nonlinear analysis.
If a linear analysis is performed, the nodal point temperature Ti is assumed to be the
component temperature as defined by the system variant $PARAMETER COMPTEMP.
8. If the function identifier is omitted or equal zero the function is replaced by the constant
value 1.0, leading to a constant convective film coefficient α = α0 .

Remarks:

4. Data input is provided for two surfaces corresponding with the upper and lower surface
of an underlying shell or membrane element (Repetition = 2). The first occurence of a
field belongs to the convection/radiation on the upper surface, the second occurence to
the convection/radiation on the lower surface of the corresponding shell or membrane
element. The orientation of the convection/radiation element is meaningless in this case.

DAT
System

extended data list. If NODES = ALL is specified, for field TFILM an extended data list is
not possible.

α = α0

α = α0 f(Ti , TF,i , t)

Remarks:
1. Names of Geometrical Data Records must be unique within one component.
2. Each data list must contain at least one item; empty lists are not allowed.
3. Trailing zeros in data lists may be omitted.

DAT
System

4. The selection of controller functions is done by irtype where the information is coded
decimally. A value greater than zero means that the corresponding functionality is taken
into account, zero means omitting the corresponding functionality. The meaning of the
decimal places depends on the controller type:
• Three-term controller (element type CONTRL5):
1.. Proportional response (always needed).
.1. Additional integral response part.
..1 Additional differential response part.
Therefore, irtype = 111 means a complete three-term controller (proportional plus
reset plus derivative controller).
• Cascade controller (element type CONTRL8 or CONTRL10):
0.... Position controller entirely omitted.
1.... Position controller included.
.0... Velocity controller entirely omitted.
.1... Velocity controller without integral response part.
.2... Velocity controller with integral response part.
..0.. Acceleration controller omitted, replaced by internal connection.
..1.. Acceleration controller without integral response part (only CONTRL10).
..2.. Acceleration controller with integral response part (only CONTRL10).
...0. Internal connection; dummy part not available.
....0 Current controller omitted, replaced by internal connection.
....1 Current controller included.
5. According to the selection of controller functions, the input values for a three-term controller (element CONTRL5) must fulfill the following conditions:
• The proportional control factor KP must be always greater than zero.
• If integral response is included, reset time TN must be greater than zero.
• If differential response is included, derivative rate time TV must be greater than or
equal zero.
• The time constant of first order delay TS must be greater than or equal zero.
• The control system scaling factor KC must be always greater than zero.

7. For cascade controllers, the nominal value and its derivatives may be requested independent from each other by nreq where the information is coded decimally. The meaning of
the decimal places is given below:
..1 Nominal displacement requested.
.1. Nominal velocity (derivative of nominal displacement) requested, .
.2. Nominal velocity as separate input requested.
1.. Nominal acceleration (second derivative of nominal displacement) requested
(only CONTRL10).
8. According to the selection of controller functions, the input values for a cascade controller
element of type CONTRL8 must fulfill the following conditions:
• If the position controller is included, its proportional factor KP d must be greater than
zero.
• The velocity controller must be always included, and its proportional factor KP v must
be greater than zero.
• If the integral response part of the velocity controller is included, the reset time TN v
must be greater than zero.
• If the current controller is omitted, it is replaced by an internal connection without
any influence.
• If the current controller is included, its equivalent time constant TE must be greater
than zero.
• Mass m used for normalization must be greater than zero.
• If nominal velocity is requested, the proportional factor of velocity feedforward Kvv ,
if specified, must be greater than zero.
• A proportional factor for velocity feedforward Kvv > 0 is possible only if nominal
velocity is requested.
• First order delay of nominal displacement is only possible if position controller is
included and nominal displacement is requested.
• If specified, the time constant TSd for first order delay of nominal displacement must
be greater or equal zero where zero means no delay.
• If specified, the time constant Tdif f for first order delay of actual velocity must be
greater or equal zero where zero means no delay.

2. Each data list must contain at least one item; empty lists are not allowed.
3. Trailing zeros in data lists may be omitted.
4. The control element may introduce nonlinear or linear, optionally frequency or speed
dependent forces or any combination of it.
5. At least one of the field pairs FUNCTION and VAR, STIFFLIN and STIFFKND or DAMPLIN
and DAMPKND must be defined.
6. The nonlinear behavior of the control element as well as dependencies of matrix elements
are defined by general functions, which must be input within a data block $FUNCTION,
see page 3-1112 ff..

7. Repetition = 15 means that up to 15 fields VAR may be used to declare independent
variables for the functions defining the nonlinear element characteristics as well as frequency and speed dependency. The sequence of VAR-fields defines the sequence of
independent variables, i.e. the i-th field VAR belongs to the i-th variable, and the sequence is valid for all nonlinear force functions in field FUNCTION.
8. For elnid > 0, fields VAR declare displacements or velocities at the element nodes P1 to
P3 as independent variables of the functions.
9. For elnid = 0, the following node-indendent data may be inserted as independent variables:

10. Nonlinear force function identifier fun = 0 or omitting trailing function identifiers means
that the corresponding nonlinear natural force is equal zero. Stiffness and damping contribution for that degree of freedom, if defined, are nevertheless included.

The matrix input is done columnwise, for diagonal matrices only the diagonal, for symmetric matrices only the upper triangle is input. Trailing zeroes may be omitted. The
symmetric part of the stiffness matrix must be positive (semi-)definite.
12. The structural damping matrix is established by multiplying each element of the stiffness
matrix by the corresponding structural damping factor. Therefore, the following rules must
be fulfilled:
• Input of structural damping factors is possible if and only if the constant stiffness
matrix is specified.
• The kind of the structural damping matrix (diagonal, symmetric or quadratic) is always the same as the kind of the stiffness matrix, i.e. it is given by stf knd.
For analyses in time domain, e.g. for time history analysis, structural damping is converted to equivalent viscous damping by

3.2 Model Data

$GEODAT CONTROLW

The reference frequency fE must be defined within the selected system variant by parameter RFREQE, see data block $PARAMETER, page 3-549.
13. For static analysis or real eigenvalue calculation, only the symmetric part of the constant
stiffness matrix in field STIFFLIN is taken into account.
14. For dynamic response or complex eigenvalue analyses, constant stiffness or damping
matrix elements may be replaced by frequency and/or rotational speed dependent functions. To do so, the following rules must be observed:
• Field STIFFFUN with stiffness function identifiers may be specified if and only if
constant stiffness matrix is given in field STIFFLIN.

• Field GFUN with structural damping factor function identifiers may be specified if and
only if constant stiffness matrix is given in field STIFFLIN. Field G, however, may be
missing.
• The sequence of function identifiers in fields STIFFFUN, DAMPFUN and GFUN corresponds to the sequence of matrix elements in fields STIFFLIN and DAMPLIN, i.e.
the i-th function identifier in field STIFFFUN replaces the i-th matrix element in field
STIFFLIN etc.. Function identifiers equal zero are ignored.
• Stiffness and viscous damping functions may be frequency and/or speed dependent,
structural damping factor functions only frequency dependent. The independent variables frequency and rotational speed must be declared by means of fields VAR.
• If a field VAR specifies frequency as independent variable, all specified stiffness,
viscous damping and structural damping factor functions must be frequency dependent. If a field VAR specifies rotational speed as independent variable, all specified
stiffness and viscous damping functions must be speed dependent. The sequence
of frequency and speed specification by fields VAR fixes the sequence of those independent variables for stiffness and viscous damping functions, and all other independent variables declared in the remaining fields VAR are ignored for those functions.
15. For time history analysis, the nonlinear force functions in field FUNCTION determine the
complete natural element forces. If, for any natural degree of freedom, no nonlinear force
function is defined, then the corresponding natural force is calculated from stiffness and
damping matrices, if those matrices are input.
16. If frequency is specified as independent variable, the corresponding value is determined
according to following rules:
• For matrix assembly in frequency domain:
– If the solution procedure performs a loop over excitation frequency, the actual
excitation frequency is used.
– If the UCI-command provides the specification of a reference frequency, the
reference frequency is specified by the command.
• For matrix assembly in time domain:

• Field DAMPFUN with viscous damping function identifiers may be specified if and
only if constant viscous damping matrix is given in field DAMPLIN.

– The reference frequency must be input in the aligned result variant by parameter

17. If rotational speed is specified as independent variable, its value must be input within the
aligned result variant by a data block $ROTSPEED (see page 3-1066 ff.) with one value.
If, however, the solution procedure performs a loop over rotational speeds (e.g. MODAL

5. The artificial stiffness for inplane rotations of shell elements is given by
Kφ,z = (0.01 + c) ∗ KB
where KB is a mean value of the bending stiffness. c = −0.01 means no artificial stiffness.

Kφ,z = (0.001 + c) ∗ KD

where KD is a mean value of the diagonal bending stiffness. c = −0.001 means no
artificial stiffness.

7. If weld spot functional dependency is specified, then the spring element represents, together with multipoint constraints of type WLDSURFACE $MPC WLDSURFACE (see

3.2 Model Data

$INISTATE

Initial State from Nonlinear Static Analysis
The initial state for a nonlinear analysis is defined by the final state of another analysis, e.g. a
nonlinear static analysis.
$INISTATE

DAT
System

Data lines:

SITUATION = name

Item(s)

Type

Explanation

name

name

Name of situation.

Remarks:
1. Definition of the initial state for an analysis is only possible within a system variant of a
single or top component.
2. All data describing the actual state of the structure, especially the deformed geometry
and the internal load distribution, are taken from the final state of the analysis perfomed
within the specified situation which should belong to a nonlinear static analysis.
3. In the case of a nonlinear static analysis the situation using the $INISTATE definition must
have a nonlinear load history, too.
4. If a situation is specified which belongs to a linear analysis, then the original state as defined by input is used as initial state. The referenced linear analysis must have generated
unique element stresses or strains, i.e. a single load pattern or result time.
5. The system variant of the specified situation must be included by a $INSERT VARIANT
data block.
6. Since the internal loading state is completely defined by the results of the specified situation, a further load state definition by a $ELSTATE LOAD data block is not allowed.
Furthermore, no other additional data blocks are possible within the actual system variant.
7. Each situation to which the initial state refers must have the same constraint variant.

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-523

$INISTATE

3 Data Input (DAT)

Please refer to MNL3, MNL4 and NLS4 of [um550].

SITUATION = NL_STEP_A

$INSERT VARIANT

Insertion of Data of Another System Variant
All data inputted for another system variant are inserted into current system variant
$INSERT VARIANT

Data lines:
(

) 

CLEAROLD =

Item(s)

Type

Explanation

sysvar

name

Name of the system variant containing the data to be inserted.

CLEAROLD

name

Clearflag for data objects in system variant varname. See remark
4.

sysvar

YES
NO

DAT
System



Remarks:
1. All data inputted for the system variant sysvar are taken over for the current system
variant. Both variants must belong to the same component. Since the system variant
of a top component fixes the system variants of all components within the configuration,
insertion of variant data is restricted to single or top components.
2. Since the referenced system variant must be a complete variant, only additional properties can be specified within the new variant. In general, overwriting of already existing
input data is not allowed. Following data blocks are possible:

V 19.00.287

PERMAS User’s Reference Manual (EDU)

3-525

$INSERT VARIANT
$ADDMATRIX
$ADDMODES
$COMPDAMP
$ELSTATE LOAD
$ELSTATE TEMP

$MODDAMP
$MODDAMPMAT
$INISTATE

3 Data Input (DAT)

Defines additional system matrices to be generated, see page
3-393.
Defines additional static mode shapes, see page 3-395.
Viscous or structural overall damping, see page 3-401.
Definition of constant element load state for generation of loaddependent system matrices, see page 3-430.
Definition of element temperature values with SOURCE=NLLOAD
for generation of temperature-dependent system matrices, see
page 3-440.
Viscous or structural modal damping, see page 3-537.
Viscous or structural modal damping matrix, see page 3-541.
Initial state for system matrices, see page 3-523. If specified, no
other additional properties may be included in the new variant.

DAT
System

$COMPDAMP, $MODDAMP and $MODDAMPMAT are only available if the new system
variant belongs to a child situation, or in a real eigenvalue analysis. As an exception,
damping data may overwrite existing data of the inserted variant. In a child situation,
however, no other data blocks may be specified within that system variant.
3. Only one level of insertion is available, recursive insertion of system variants is not possible.
4. If referenced and new system variant are used in situations where they are connected
to the same constraint variant, system matrices generated within the referenced system
variant are used directly within the new system variant. If, due to additional input, some
matrices are generated for the new system variant anew, the corresponding matrices
of the referenced system variant are deleted by default (CLEAROLD = YES) to save
disk storage. Specifying CLEAROLD = NO retains all matrices. The system module
belonging to the referenced system variant must not be cleared (e.g. by UCI-statement
CLEAR SYSTEM).
5. Modal frequency or transient response analyses may be performed using a system variant where the system variant of the corresponding parent situation is inserted and only
damping specification is added.
6. If system matrices of the referenced system variant are used directly, the actual state of
the matrices is used. This is important e.g. in nonlinear calculations.

Remarks:
1. The $MATREF defines physically one of the eigen systems of the second rank structure
tensor of the fiber orientation distribution, so this command is not compatible with structure tensor input $ELSTATE STCTENS, only one of them can be specified for a single
element to describe the reference direction.
2. A material reference system has to be defined for all membrane, shell and solid elements
with non-isotropic material.
3. For gasket elements, the material reference system is derived from the element system,
therefore a definition by $MATREF is not possible. The element system, however, must
be defined within the $STRUCTURE bracket.
4. The coordinates of points may be given in the component system (default) or in any other
reference system rsys, which may be a cartesian, cylindrical or spherical one.
5. Angles must be input in degrees.
6. If RSYS is specified on the header line, the given reference system rsys is used to establish the material reference system. Reference systems are defined by data blocks
$RSYS, whereat RSYS = 0 means the component system.
The behavior for 2-dimensional elements is described in remark 7. Otherwise for cylindrical or spherical reference systems the local cartesian system for the orientation of the
element local system is generated at the element center of gravity using the generation
rules defined on page 1-11.
If parameter AXES is omitted, the local element system coincides with the local cartesian
system, else idof x specifies the axis of the local cartesian system which is used as xaxis of the material reference system, and idof y specifies the axis of the local cartesian
system which is used as y-axis of the material reference system. Following values may
be used:
1
(-1) : positive (negative) x-axis of reference system.
2
(-2) : positive (negative) y-axis of reference system.
3
(-3) : positive (negative) z-axis of reference system.

7. If RSYS or POINTS is specified on the header line and 2-dimensional non-axisymmetric
elements with non-isotropic material behavior are referred (e.g. SHELL3/4), the material
reference system is established by a projection method of the assembled local cartesian

The corresponding x-axis of the local cartesian system and the element normal direction

UCI-switch TOLPHI.
The material m1 -direction is defined by the intersection of the element reference plane
and the plane spanned by the element normal direction and the x-axis of the local cartesian system. The material m3 -direction is always given by the element normal direction
and the material m2 -direction is then calculated to form a right-hand-system.

$MATREF

Definition of Material Reference System by Using three Points

The three non-collinear points P1 , P2 and P3 fix the reference directions (m1 m2 m3 ) for anisotropic material data in the following way:

1. The m1 -direction is parallel to the xr -axis which is directed from point P1 to point P2 .
2. The m2 -direction is parallel to the yr -axis which is normal to the xr -axis and oriented
towards point P3 .
3. The m3 -direction is normal to m1 and m2 , constituting a right-hand system.
For 2-dimensional elements this system is projected onto the element reference plane, see
remark 7.

The user has to input the switch variable iswit, which defines a reference direction in the
element reference plane, and the angle γ. For iswit = 0 the e1 -axis of the local element system
is used as reference direction, for iswit > 0 the reference direction is given by the intersection
line of the element reference plane with a plane defined by two of the three coordinate axes
of component system. Rotating by angle γ around e3 which is parallel to the element normal
leads to the material 1-direction m1 . The m1 -axis of the local plane material reference system
is parallel to the material 1-direction. The second axis m2 together with m1 and e3 form a
right-hand system (m1 , m2 , e3 ).

Remarks:
1. Modal damping may be used only if modal degrees of freedom exist, otherwise an error
occurs. It may be defined only for single or top components and, in addition, for subcomponentes with dynamic (e.g. Craig-Bampton) condensation. It is available also in
system variants of child situations where data from another system variant are inserted,
see $INSERT VARIANT, page 3-525.
2. If modal damping is input by a $MODDAMPMAT data block, then the input of corresponding modal viscous or structural damping by a $MODDAMP data block is not possible for
the same degree of freedom.
3. For coupled analysis, modal damping must be inputted for degree of freedom type MATH.
Modal damping for other degree of freedom types are neglected.
4. A complete viscous or structural damping matrix in modal space may be defined, i.e.
modal damping for each mode as well as cross coupling terms. The identifiers i and
j refer to rows and columns of the damping matrix in modal space, i.e. they count the
generalized degrees of freedom given by elastic eigenmodes and, if any, additional static
mode shapes and singular (e.g. rigid body) modes (counted in that sequence).
5. If the indices i and j are omitted, then the damping definition is valid for all diagonal values
of the viscous or structural damping matrix in modal space.
6. Attention: Please keep in mind that the sign of mode shapes is not uniquely defined
and that for clusters of eigenfrequencies only the subspace of eigenmodes may be determined; so eigenmodes of the same model but different runs may differ, and so it is
strongly recommended to use only the eigenmodes of the actual run to calculate offdiagonal modal damping input data. For diagonal modal damping input data, the sign
of eigenmodes doesn’t matter, the shapes of eigenmodes within a cluster (e.g. due to
symmetry), however, must be taken into account.
7. The format of the specified damping matrix in modal space must be defined by parameter
FORMAT, it may be diagonal, symmetric or rectangular (nonsymmetric). If the input of
a viscous or structural damping matrix in modal space is split, the first $MODDAMPMAT

13. If TYPE = G is specified, the coefficients gii represent the imaginary part of complex
stiffness term given by
k̄ii = (1 + i gii )kii
with the modal stiffness kii of the elastic eigenmode i. Since the mode shapes are
stiffness-orthonormalized, it holds kii = 1.0, and the coefficients gii are inserted directly
into the modal structural damping matrix. The same is done with the off-diagonal coefficients gij .
Modal structural damping is available for displacement degrees of freedom only.
Input of damping coefficients is possible for elastic eigenmodes as well as for additional
static mode shapes, but not for singular (e.g. rigid body) modes or additional static mode
shapes representing internally defined state variables.

displacement degrees of freedom of the interface elements and the pressure degrees of
freedom of the fluid surface nodes. All pressure degrees of freedom of the interface elements must be dependent, and all pressure degrees of freedom of the fluid surface nodes
must be local or prescribed.

i
X h
Lc =
ci LS,i + LT,i (ci T ) + Lδ,i (ci δU ) + LΩ,i (ci Ω)

3-564

3.2 Model Data

$COMBINE LOADS

where LS,i contains all scalable parts (loads proportional to input values directly) of load
pattern i, LT,i contains all temperature-dependent load parts, Lδ,i contains all gapwidthdependent contact loads and LΩ,i contains all load parts depending on rotational velocity
Ω.
4. Note that $COMBINE LOADS builds up a new load by combining/scaling the input values
from other load patterns rather than combining/scaling the assembled load vectors:
• E.g. this will scale the temperature values T instead of the corresponding temperature strains εϑ = α (T − T0 ) or scale the additive gap width δU instead of the
corresponding initial gap width δ0 = δgeo + δU .
– LT,i (ci = 0)6=0 if the reference temperature T0 and/or Tref is not zero.
– Lδ,i (ci = 0)6=0 if geometrical gap δgeo 6= 0 and $CONTACT LOAD uses GAPWIDTH = ADD.
• In general (even for a linear static analysis) the result of a combined load pattern differs from the superposition of the corresponding load pattern results, see
$COMBINE RESULTS (see page 3-1003 ff.)
• An alternative approach is offered by $NLLOAD (see page 3-838 ff.).
5. Combining load patterns, any number of loads of the same type may be accumulated with
the following restrictions:
• Since temperatures must be unique, only one temperature load definition per element may exist for each combined load pattern.
• Only one definition for each kind of inertia loads by $INERTIA (see page 3-820 ff.)
or $INERTIAX (see page 3-823 ff.) is possible for each element in each combined
load pattern.
• Only one surrounding temperature definition per element may contribute to each
combined load pattern. The surrounding temperatures in the remaining load patterns
referred by the combined load pattern must be set to zero.
6. Contact load property values defined by $CONTACT LOAD (see page 3-567 ff.) may be
combined according to following rules:
• Contact load property values must be valid for all contacts belonging to the specified
contact identifier or name, i.e. node identifier nid on data lines defining contact load
properties must not be used (see page 3-573, remark 7).
• For any contact identifier or contact name, the contact load property parameter
GAPWIDTH must be identical specified for each load pattern to be combined.
• Moreover we recommend identical specifications in all combined load patterns for
the load property parameters NORMAL and FRICTION (or make use of the ’neutral’
definitions NORMAL=FREE and FRICTION=FREE respectively).
However, for special purposes it is also possible to combine contact loads with nonmatching NORMAL or FRICTION parameter. For a description of sensible combinations and resulting contact parameters see page 4-2ff. of [um550]

• If the combined load represents a stochastic load, then the dependency of friction
coefficients on basic variables must be unique, and therefore only one value 6= 0 is
accepted for each datum; the values in the remaining load patterns to be combined
must be set to zero. GAPWIDTH = ADD (input of additive gap widths) is not possible

7. If for any load pattern a basic variable identifier bsvid (instead of a constant factor c) is
specified, then the combined load pattern represents a stochastic load and may be used
in reliability analysis.
8. Any number of combined load patterns may be defined, but only one combined load
pattern may represent a stochastic load.
9. Basic variables used to establish stochastic loads must be declared as load factors, see
$BASVAR (see page 3-29 ff.).
10. Within the definition of a combined load pattern, each load pattern and each basic variable
may appear only once.
11. Combination of already combined load patterns are not possible.
12. Combined load patterns may not contain any directly defined loads.

Remarks:
1. $CONTVAL is a name alias to $CONTACT LOAD provided for backward compatibility
as well as ISO and ANISO are name aliases to the FRICTION types COULOMB and
COULOMB,COULOMB , respectively.
2. Definition of contact load properties is only possible within a loading variant of a top or
single components.
3. Each contact load refers to a corresponding $CONTACT NODE or $CONTACT SURFACE
definition made in the constraint variant.
4. If no contact load property is given for a certain contact definition respectively load pattern,
the ’neutral’ default definition GAPWIDTH = ABS with δU = 0.0, NORMAL = FREE and
FRICTION = FREE is used (note that this differs from the default NORMAL = CALCULATE
when the NORMAL parameter is omitted for a given $CONTACT LOAD).
5. If for the friction type parameter FRICTION only one parameter is specified, it is assumed
that it holds for all tangential directions specified in the corresponding contact definition,
see remark 3. If two tangential directions are specified and if they should be treated different, the first parameter specifies the friction type for the first tangential yC -direction and
the second parameter specifies the friction type for the second tangential zC -direction.
6. Each data line defines one set of contact load properties for one loading case. They
are assigned to all contacts belonging to the specified contact identifier / contact name or,

contact identifier / name, one loading case and one node only one definition of contact
load properties is possible.
7. If the node identifier / node set nid/nset is omitted, the contact load properties are assigned to all contacts belonging to the specified contact identifier / contact name.

9. For contact to ground, only GAPWIDTH = ABS is meaningful. Since the geometry of
the second partner is not defined, the geometrical gap width δgeo is set to zero. For
clarification see the results of surface to ground contact in example CA4.
10. If GAPWIDTH = ABS is specified, the initial gap width is given by
δ0 = δU
neglecting the geometrical distance of the contact points.
11. If GAPWIDTH = ADD is specified, the initial gap width δ0 is given by
δ0 = δgeo + δU
where δU is the user-defined initial gap width and δgeo is the geometrical gap width, i.e.
the x-coordinate (contact normal direction) of the second contact node in the contact
coordinate system.

δ0 = (δgeo −δtouch ) + δU
where δtouch is the minimum δgeo value of all contact pairs within the same contact definition. E.g. a user value δU = 0.0 brings an all-passive contact partner into first relative
contact or shifts the gap values of a geometrically penetrating partner to a virtually nonpenetrating state, respectively.

17. If one special argument is selected via f argδ then only that variable is passed as independent variable to the load function. This is usefull to pass other arguments than
just xn to load functions with one independent variable only, e.g. f argδ =z for sin(zn ).
If f argδ is a text string with a comma separated list of arguments then only these arguments are passed to the load function (in given sequence), e.g. f argδ = ’z,dg,nid’ or
f argδ = ’(z,dg,nid)’.
For non-cartesian reference systems the alternative f argδ symbols R, PHI and THETA
may be used for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd coordinate, respectively.
18. If a scale factor is specified by parameter FACTOR, all floating point values of the current
data block are multiplied by the given value factor, i.e. the same scaling applies to δU as
well as to µ0 , µ1 or Rp (if given).
19. If NORMAL = FREE is specified, then the contact is always open, i.e. it is entirely omitted.
20. If NORMAL = FIXED is specified, contact forces will be introduced to close the contact
and always keep it at δ = 0.0. Thus the contact forces in normal direction may become
negative, e.g. if the gap was initially open.
21. If NORMAL = FIXED_OR_FREE , FIXED_IF_ACTIVE or FREE_IF_PASSIVE is specified in a contact analysis with non-linear load history (see $NLLOAD and $NLRESULTS)
it is ignored in the first load step and treated as NORMAL = CALCULATE. Afterwards
the status stays FIXED respectively FREE for all subsequent load steps as soon as the
contact has closed respectively opened once. Contact pairs which have not been set
to FIXED respectively FREE are treated as NORMAL = CALCULATE in the current load
step.
For a standard static analysis (independent load patterns without load history) this has
no effect, i.e. all three settings behave as if NORMAL = CALCULATE would have been
specified.
22. If NORMAL = FORCE is specified the contact stays active and will constantly transmit
the prescribed force Rp at each contact pair. Thus the gap width may become nonzero or even negative depending on the given load and surrounding stiffness. The pre-

* Note that PHI and THETA are swapped for spherical f rsys with $RSYS SPHERE.
